lines.text: Alarum. Enter Duke of York, Edward, Richard, Norfolk, Montague, Warwick and Soldiers, all wearing the white rose.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I wonder how the King escaped our hands.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: While we pursued the horsemen of the north,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: He slyly stole away and left his men;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Whereat the great Lord of Northumberland,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Whose warlike ears could never brook retreat,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Cheered up the drooping army; and himself,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Lord Clifford, and Lord Stafford, all abreast,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Charged our main battle’s front, and breaking in,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Were by the swords of common soldiers slain.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Lord Stafford’s father, Duke of Buckingham,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Is either slain or wounded dangerous;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: I cleft his beaver with a downright blow.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: That this is true, father, behold his blood.
[_Showing his bloody sword._]

lines.speaker: MONTAGUE
lines.text: And, brother, here’s the Earl of Wiltshire’s blood,
[_To York, showing his._]

lines.speaker: MONTAGUE
lines.text: Whom I encountered as the battles joined.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Speak thou for me, and tell them what I did.
[_Throwing down the Duke of Somerset’s head._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Richard hath best deserved of all my sons.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: But is your Grace dead, my Lord of Somerset?

lines.speaker: NORFOLK
lines.text: Such hope have all the line of John of Gaunt!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Thus do I hope to shake King Henry’s head.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And so do I. Victorious Prince of York,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Before I see thee seated in that throne

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Which now the house of Lancaster usurps,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I vow by heaven these eyes shall never close.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: This is the palace of the fearful king,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And this the regal seat. Possess it, York,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For this is thine, and not King Henry’s heirs’.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Assist me, then, sweet Warwick, and I will;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: For hither we have broken in by force.

lines.speaker: NORFOLK
lines.text: We’ll all assist you; he that flies shall die.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Thanks, gentle Norfolk. Stay by me, my lords;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And, soldiers, stay and lodge by me this night.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And when the King comes, offer him no violence,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Unless he seek to thrust you out perforce.
[_They retire._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The Queen this day here holds her parliament,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: But little thinks we shall be of her council.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: By words or blows here let us win our right.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Armed as we are, let’s stay within this house.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: The bloody parliament shall this be called,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Unless Plantagenet, Duke of York, be king,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And bashful Henry deposed, whose cowardice

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Hath made us bywords to our enemies.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Then leave me not, my lords; be resolute.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I mean to take possession of my right.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Neither the King, nor he that loves him best,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: The proudest he that holds up Lancaster,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Dares stir a wing if Warwick shake his bells.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I’ll plant Plantagenet, root him up who dares.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Resolve thee, Richard; claim the English crown.
[_Warwick leads York to the throne, who seats himself._]
Flourish. Enter King Henry, Clifford, Northumberland, Westmoreland, Exeter and the rest, all wearing the red rose.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My lords, look where the sturdy rebel sits,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Even in the chair of state! Belike he means,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Backed by the power of Warwick, that false peer,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To aspire unto the crown and reign as king.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Earl of Northumberland, he slew thy father,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And thine, Lord Clifford; and you both have vowed revenge

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: On him, his sons, his favourites, and his friends.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: If I be not, heavens be revenged on me!

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: The hope thereof makes Clifford mourn in steel.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: What, shall we suffer this? Let’s pluck him down.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: My heart for anger burns. I cannot brook it.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Be patient, gentle Earl of Westmoreland.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Patience is for poltroons, such as he.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: He durst not sit there had your father lived.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: My gracious lord, here in the parliament

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Let us assail the family of York.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Well hast thou spoken, cousin. Be it so.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ah, know you not the city favours them,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And they have troops of soldiers at their beck?

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: But when the Duke is slain, they’ll quickly fly.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Far be the thought of this from Henry’s heart,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To make a shambles of the Parliament House!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Cousin of Exeter, frowns, words, and threats

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Shall be the war that Henry means to use.
[_They advance to the Duke._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thou factious Duke of York, descend my throne,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And kneel for grace and mercy at my feet;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I am thy sovereign.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I am thine.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: For shame, come down. He made thee Duke of York.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: ’Twas my inheritance, as the earldom was.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Thy father was a traitor to the crown.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Exeter, thou art a traitor to the crown

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: In following this usurping Henry.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Whom should he follow but his natural king?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: True, Clifford, that’s Richard, Duke of York.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And shall I stand, and thou sit in my throne?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: It must and shall be so. Content thyself.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Be Duke of Lancaster. Let him be king.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: He is both King and Duke of Lancaster;

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: And that the Lord of Westmoreland shall maintain.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And Warwick shall disprove it. You forget

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That we are those which chased you from the field

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And slew your fathers, and with colours spread

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Marched through the city to the palace gates.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Yes, Warwick, I remember it to my grief;

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And, by his soul, thou and thy house shall rue it.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Plantagenet, of thee and these thy sons,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Thy kinsmen, and thy friends, I’ll have more lives

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Than drops of blood were in my father’s veins.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Urge it no more; lest that, instead of words,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: I send thee, Warwick, such a messenger

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: As shall revenge his death before I stir.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Poor Clifford, how I scorn his worthless threats!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Will you we show our title to the crown?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: If not, our swords shall plead it in the field.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What title hast thou, traitor, to the crown?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thy father was, as thou art, Duke of York;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thy grandfather, Roger Mortimer, Earl of March.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I am the son of Henry the Fifth,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Who made the Dauphin and the French to stoop,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And seized upon their towns and provinces.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Talk not of France, sith thou hast lost it all.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The Lord Protector lost it, and not I.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: When I was crowned I was but nine months old.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: You are old enough now, and yet, methinks, you lose.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Father, tear the crown from the usurper’s head.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Sweet father, do so; set it on your head.

lines.speaker: MONTAGUE
lines.text: Good brother, as thou lov’st and honourest arms,

lines.speaker: MONTAGUE
lines.text: Let’s fight it out and not stand cavilling thus.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Sound drums and trumpets, and the King will fly.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Sons, peace!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Peace thou, and give King Henry leave to speak.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Plantagenet shall speak first. Hear him, lords,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And be you silent and attentive too,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For he that interrupts him shall not live.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Think’st thou that I will leave my kingly throne,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Wherein my grandsire and my father sat?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No. First shall war unpeople this my realm;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ay, and their colours, often borne in France,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And now in England, to our heart’s great sorrow,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Shall be my winding-sheet. Why faint you, lords?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My title’s good, and better far than his.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Prove it, Henry, and thou shalt be king.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Henry the Fourth by conquest got the crown.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: ’Twas by rebellion against his king.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I know not what to say; my title’s weak.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Tell me, may not a king adopt an heir?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: What then?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: An if he may, then am I lawful king;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For Richard, in the view of many lords,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Resigned the crown to Henry the Fourth,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whose heir my father was, and I am his.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: He rose against him, being his sovereign,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And made him to resign his crown perforce.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Suppose, my lords, he did it unconstrained,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Think you ’twere prejudicial to his crown?

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: No, for he could not so resign his crown

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: But that the next heir should succeed and reign.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Art thou against us, Duke of Exeter?

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: His is the right, and therefore pardon me.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Why whisper you, my lords, and answer not?

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: My conscience tells me he is lawful king.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: All will revolt from me and turn to him.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Plantagenet, for all the claim thou lay’st,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Think not that Henry shall be so deposed.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Deposed he shall be, in despite of all.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Thou art deceived. ’Tis not thy southern power,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Of Essex, Norfolk, Suffolk, nor of Kent,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Which makes thee thus presumptuous and proud,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Can set the Duke up in despite of me.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: King Henry, be thy title right or wrong,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Lord Clifford vows to fight in thy defence.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: May that ground gape and swallow me alive,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Where I shall kneel to him that slew my father!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O Clifford, how thy words revive my heart!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Henry of Lancaster, resign thy crown.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: What mutter you, or what conspire you, lords?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Do right unto this princely Duke of York,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Or I will fill the house with armed men,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And over the chair of state where now he sits,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Write up his title with usurping blood.
[_He stamps with his foot, and the Soldiers show themselves._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My Lord of Warwick, hear but one word:

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Let me for this my lifetime reign as king.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Confirm the crown to me, and to mine heirs,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And thou shalt reign in quiet while thou liv’st.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I am content. Richard Plantagenet,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Enjoy the kingdom after my decease.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: What wrong is this unto the Prince your son!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: What good is this to England and himself!

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Base, fearful, and despairing Henry!

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: How hast thou injured both thyself and us!

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: I cannot stay to hear these articles.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Nor I.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Come, cousin, let us tell the Queen these news.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Farewell, faint-hearted and degenerate king,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: In whose cold blood no spark of honour bides.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Be thou a prey unto the house of York,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And die in bands for this unmanly deed!

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: In dreadful war mayst thou be overcome,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Or live in peace abandoned and despised!
[_Exeunt Westmoreland, Northumberland and Clifford._]

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Turn this way, Henry, and regard them not.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: They seek revenge, and therefore will not yield.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ah, Exeter!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Why should you sigh, my lord?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Not for myself, Lord Warwick, but my son,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whom I unnaturally shall disinherit.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But be it as it may, [_To York._] I here entail

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The crown to thee and to thine heirs for ever;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Conditionally, that here thou take an oath

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To cease this civil war, and whilst I live,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To honour me as thy king and sovereign,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And neither by treason nor hostility

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To seek to put me down and reign thyself.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: This oath I willingly take and will perform.
[_Coming from the throne._]

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Long live King Henry! Plantagenet, embrace him.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And long live thou, and these thy forward sons!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Now York and Lancaster are reconciled.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Accursed be he that seeks to make them foes!
Sennet. Here they come down.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Farewell, my gracious lord. I’ll to my castle.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And I’ll keep London with my soldiers.

lines.speaker: NORFOLK
lines.text: And I to Norfolk with my followers.

lines.speaker: MONTAGUE
lines.text: And I unto the sea from whence I came.
[_Exeunt York and his Sons, Warwick, Norfolk, Montague and their Soldiers._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And I with grief and sorrow to the court.
Enter Queen Margaret and the Prince of Wales.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Here comes the Queen, whose looks bewray her anger.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: I’ll steal away.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Exeter, so will I.
[_Going._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Nay, go not from me; I will follow thee.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Be patient, gentle Queen, and I will stay.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Who can be patient in such extremes?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ah, wretched man, would I had died a maid,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And never seen thee, never borne thee son,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Seeing thou hast proved so unnatural a father.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Hath he deserved to lose his birthright thus?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Hadst thou but loved him half so well as I,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Or felt that pain which I did for him once,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Or nourished him as I did with my blood,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thou wouldst have left thy dearest heart-blood there,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Rather than have made that savage duke thine heir

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And disinherited thine only son.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Father, you cannot disinherit me.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: If you be king, why should not I succeed?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Pardon me, Margaret; pardon me, sweet son.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The Earl of Warwick and the Duke enforced me.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Enforced thee! Art thou King, and wilt be forced?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I shame to hear thee speak. Ah, timorous wretch,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thou hast undone thyself, thy son, and me,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And given unto the house of York such head

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: As thou shalt reign but by their sufferance.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: To entail him and his heirs unto the crown,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What is it but to make thy sepulchre

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And creep into it far before thy time?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Warwick is Chancellor and the lord of Calais;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Stern Falconbridge commands the narrow seas;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The Duke is made Protector of the realm;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And yet shalt thou be safe? Such safety finds

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The trembling lamb environed with wolves.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Had I been there, which am a silly woman,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The soldiers should have tossed me on their pikes

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Before I would have granted to that act.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But thou prefer’st thy life before thine honour.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And seeing thou dost, I here divorce myself

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Both from thy table, Henry, and thy bed,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Until that act of parliament be repealed

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Whereby my son is disinherited.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The northern lords that have forsworn thy colours

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Will follow mine if once they see them spread;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And spread they shall be, to thy foul disgrace

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And utter ruin of the house of York.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thus do I leave thee. Come, son, let’s away:

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Our army is ready; come, we’ll after them.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Stay, gentle Margaret, and hear me speak.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thou hast spoke too much already. Get thee gone.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Gentle son Edward, thou wilt stay with me?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ay, to be murdered by his enemies.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: When I return with victory from the field

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: I’ll see your Grace. Till then I’ll follow her.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Come, son, away; we may not linger thus.
[_Exeunt Queen Margaret and the Prince._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Poor queen! How love to me and to her son

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Hath made her break out into terms of rage!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Revenged may she be on that hateful Duke,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whose haughty spirit, winged with desire,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Will cost my crown, and like an empty eagle

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Tire on the flesh of me and of my son.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The loss of those three lords torments my heart.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I’ll write unto them and entreat them fair.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Come, cousin, you shall be the messenger.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And I, I hope, shall reconcile them all.
[_Flourish. Exeunt._]

lines.text: Had he been slaughter-man to all my kin,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: I should not for my life but weep with him,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: To see how inly sorrow gripes his soul.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What, weeping-ripe, my Lord Northumberland?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Think but upon the wrong he did us all,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And that will quickly dry thy melting tears.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Here’s for my oath, here’s for my father’s death.
[_Stabbing him._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And here’s to right our gentle-hearted king.
[_Stabbing him._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Open thy gate of mercy, gracious God!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: My soul flies through these wounds to seek out Thee.
[_Dies._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Off with his head, and set it on York gates;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: So York may overlook the town of York.
[_Flourish. Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A plain near Mortimer’s Cross in Herefordshire

lines.text: A march. Enter Edward and Richard and their power.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: I wonder how our princely father scaped,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Or whether he be scaped away or no

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: From Clifford’s and Northumberland’s pursuit.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Had he been ta’en, we should have heard the news;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Had he been slain, we should have heard the news;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Or had he scaped, methinks we should have heard

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: The happy tidings of his good escape.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: How fares my brother? Why is he so sad?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I cannot joy until I be resolved

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Where our right valiant father is become.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I saw him in the battle range about,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And watched him how he singled Clifford forth.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Methought he bore him in the thickest troop

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: As doth a lion in a herd of neat;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Or as a bear, encompassed round with dogs,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Who having pinched a few and made them cry,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The rest stand all aloof and bark at him.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: So fared our father with his enemies;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: So fled his enemies my warlike father.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Methinks ’tis pride enough to be his son.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: See how the morning opes her golden gates

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And takes her farewell of the glorious sun.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: How well resembles it the prime of youth,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Trimmed like a younker prancing to his love!

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Dazzle mine eyes, or do I see three suns?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Three glorious suns, each one a perfect sun;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Not separated with the racking clouds,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But severed in a pale clear-shining sky.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: See, see, they join, embrace, and seem to kiss,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: As if they vowed some league inviolable.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Now are they but one lamp, one light, one sun.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: In this the heaven figures some event.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: ’Tis wondrous strange, the like yet never heard of.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: I think it cites us, brother, to the field,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: That we, the sons of brave Plantagenet,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Each one already blazing by our meeds,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Should notwithstanding join our lights together,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And overshine the earth, as this the world.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Whate’er it bodes, henceforward will I bear

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Upon my target three fair shining suns.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Nay, bear three daughters: by your leave I speak it,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: You love the breeder better than the male.
Enter a Messenger, blowing.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But what art thou, whose heavy looks foretell

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Some dreadful story hanging on thy tongue?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Ah, one that was a woeful looker-on

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: When as the noble Duke of York was slain,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Your princely father and my loving lord.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: O, speak no more, for I have heard too much!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Say how he died, for I will hear it all.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Environed he was with many foes,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And stood against them as the hope of Troy

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Against the Greeks that would have entered Troy.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: But Hercules himself must yield to odds;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And many strokes, though with a little axe,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Hews down and fell the hardest-timbered oak.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: By many hands your father was subdued,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: But only slaughtered by the ireful arm

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Of unrelenting Clifford and the Queen,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Who crowned the gracious duke in high despite,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Laughed in his face; and when with grief he wept,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The ruthless Queen gave him to dry his cheeks

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: A napkin steeped in the harmless blood

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Of sweet young Rutland, by rough Clifford slain.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And after many scorns, many foul taunts,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: They took his head, and on the gates of York

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: They set the same; and there it doth remain,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The saddest spectacle that e’er I viewed.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Sweet Duke of York, our prop to lean upon,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Now thou art gone, we have no staff, no stay.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: O Clifford, boisterous Clifford, thou hast slain

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: The flower of Europe for his chivalry;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And treacherously hast thou vanquished him,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: For hand to hand he would have vanquished thee.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Now my soul’s palace is become a prison.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Ah, would she break from hence, that this my body

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Might in the ground be closed up in rest!

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: For never henceforth shall I joy again;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Never, O, never, shall I see more joy!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I cannot weep, for all my body’s moisture

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Scarce serves to quench my furnace-burning heart;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Nor can my tongue unload my heart’s great burthen,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For selfsame wind that I should speak withal

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Is kindling coals that fires all my breast

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And burns me up with flames that tears would quench.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To weep is to make less the depth of grief:

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Tears, then, for babes; blows and revenge for me!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Richard, I bear thy name; I’ll venge thy death,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Or die renowned by attempting it.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: His name that valiant duke hath left with thee;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: His dukedom and his chair with me is left.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Nay, if thou be that princely eagle’s bird,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Show thy descent by gazing ’gainst the sun;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For chair and dukedom, throne and kingdom say,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Either that is thine, or else thou wert not his.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: March. Enter Warwick, Marquess Montague and their army.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: How now, fair lords! What fare? What news abroad?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Great Lord of Warwick, if we should recount

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Our baleful news, and at each word’s deliverance

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Stab poniards in our flesh till all were told,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The words would add more anguish than the wounds.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: O valiant lord, the Duke of York is slain!

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: O, Warwick, Warwick, that Plantagenet

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Which held thee dearly as his soul’s redemption

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Is by the stern Lord Clifford done to death.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Ten days ago I drowned these news in tears,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And now, to add more measure to your woes,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I come to tell you things sith then befall’n.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: After the bloody fray at Wakefield fought,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Where your brave father breathed his latest gasp,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Tidings, as swiftly as the posts could run,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Were brought me of your loss and his depart.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I, then in London, keeper of the King,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Mustered my soldiers, gathered flocks of friends,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And very well appointed, as I thought,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Marched toward Saint Albans to intercept the Queen,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Bearing the King in my behalf along;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For by my scouts I was advertised

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That she was coming with a full intent

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: To dash our late decree in Parliament

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Touching King Henry’s oath and your succession.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Short tale to make, we at Saint Albans met,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Our battles joined, and both sides fiercely fought.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But, whether ’twas the coldness of the King,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Who looked full gently on his warlike Queen,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That robbed my soldiers of their heated spleen,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Or whether ’twas report of her success;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Or more than common fear of Clifford’s rigour,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Who thunders to his captives blood and death,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I cannot judge; but, to conclude with truth,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Their weapons like to lightning came and went;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Our soldiers’, like the night-owl’s lazy flight,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Or like an idle thresher with a flail,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Fell gently down, as if they struck their friends.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I cheered them up with justice of our cause,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: With promise of high pay and great rewards,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But all in vain; they had no heart to fight,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And we in them no hope to win the day;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: So that we fled: the King unto the Queen;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Lord George your brother, Norfolk, and myself,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: In haste, post-haste, are come to join with you;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For in the Marches here we heard you were,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Making another head to fight again.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Where is the Duke of Norfolk, gentle Warwick?

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And when came George from Burgundy to England?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Some six miles off the Duke is with the soldiers;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And for your brother, he was lately sent

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: From your kind aunt, Duchess of Burgundy,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: With aid of soldiers to this needful war.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: ’Twas odds, belike, when valiant Warwick fled.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Oft have I heard his praises in pursuit,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But ne’er till now his scandal of retire.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Nor now my scandal, Richard, dost thou hear;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For thou shalt know this strong right hand of mine

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Can pluck the diadem from faint Henry’s head

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And wring the awful sceptre from his fist,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Were he as famous and as bold in war

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: As he is famed for mildness, peace, and prayer.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I know it well, Lord Warwick; blame me not.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: ’Tis love I bear thy glories makes me speak.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But in this troublous time what’s to be done?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Shall we go throw away our coats of steel

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And wrap our bodies in black mourning gowns,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Numbering our Ave-Maries with our beads?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Or shall we on the helmets of our foes

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Tell our devotion with revengeful arms?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: If for the last, say ay, and to it, lords.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Why, therefore Warwick came to seek you out,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And therefore comes my brother Montague.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Attend me, lords. The proud insulting Queen,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: With Clifford and the haught Northumberland,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And of their feather many moe proud birds,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Have wrought the easy-melting King like wax.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: He swore consent to your succession,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: His oath enrolled in the Parliament;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And now to London all the crew are gone,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: To frustrate both his oath and what beside

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: May make against the house of Lancaster.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Their power, I think, is thirty thousand strong.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Now, if the help of Norfolk and myself,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: With all the friends that thou, brave Earl of March,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Amongst the loving Welshmen canst procure,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Will but amount to five and twenty thousand,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Why, _via_, to London will we march amain,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And once again bestride our foaming steeds,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And once again cry “Charge upon our foes!”

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But never once again turn back and fly.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Ay, now methinks I hear great Warwick speak.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Ne’er may he live to see a sunshine day

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That cries “Retire,” if Warwick bid him stay.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Lord Warwick, on thy shoulder will I lean;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And when thou fail’st—as God forbid the hour!—

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Must Edward fall, which peril heaven forfend!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: No longer Earl of March, but Duke of York.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: The next degree is England’s royal throne;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For King of England shalt thou be proclaimed

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: In every borough as we pass along,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And he that throws not up his cap for joy

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Shall for the fault make forfeit of his head.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: King Edward, valiant Richard, Montague,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Stay we no longer dreaming of renown,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But sound the trumpets and about our task.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Then, Clifford, were thy heart as hard as steel,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: As thou hast shown it flinty by thy deeds,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I come to pierce it, or to give thee mine.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Then strike up, drums! God and Saint George for us!
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: How now, what news?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The Duke of Norfolk sends you word by me,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The Queen is coming with a puissant host,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And craves your company for speedy counsel.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Why then it sorts; brave warriors, let’s away.
[_Exeunt._]
Flourish. Enter King Henry, Queen Margaret, the Prince of Wales, Clifford and Northumberland with drums and trumpets.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Welcome, my lord, to this brave town of York.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Yonder’s the head of that arch-enemy

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: That sought to be encompassed with your crown.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Doth not the object cheer your heart, my lord?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ay, as the rocks cheer them that fear their wrack!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To see this sight, it irks my very soul.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Withhold revenge, dear God! ’Tis not my fault,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Nor wittingly have I infringed my vow.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: My gracious liege, this too much lenity

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And harmful pity must be laid aside.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: To whom do lions cast their gentle looks?

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Not to the beast that would usurp their den.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Whose hand is that the forest bear doth lick?

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Not his that spoils her young before her face.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Who scapes the lurking serpent’s mortal sting?

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Not he that sets his foot upon her back.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: The smallest worm will turn, being trodden on,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And doves will peck in safeguard of their brood.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Ambitious York did level at thy crown,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Thou smiling while he knit his angry brows.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: He, but a duke, would have his son a king,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And raise his issue like a loving sire;

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Thou, being a king, blest with a goodly son,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Didst yield consent to disinherit him,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Which argued thee a most unloving father.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Unreasonable creatures feed their young;

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And though man’s face be fearful to their eyes,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Yet, in protection of their tender ones,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Who hath not seen them, even with those wings

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Which sometime they have used with fearful flight,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Make war with him that climbed unto their nest,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Offering their own lives in their young’s defence?

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: For shame, my liege, make them your precedent.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Were it not pity that this goodly boy

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Should lose his birthright by his father’s fault,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And long hereafter say unto his child,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: “What my great-grandfather and grandsire got,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: My careless father fondly gave away?”

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Ah, what a shame were this! Look on the boy,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And let his manly face, which promiseth

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Successful fortune, steel thy melting heart

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: To hold thine own and leave thine own with him.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Full well hath Clifford played the orator,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Inferring arguments of mighty force.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But, Clifford, tell me, didst thou never hear

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That things ill got had ever bad success?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And happy always was it for that son

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whose father for his hoarding went to hell?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I’ll leave my son my virtuous deeds behind,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And would my father had left me no more;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For all the rest is held at such a rate

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: As brings a thousand-fold more care to keep

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Than in possession any jot of pleasure.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ah, cousin York, would thy best friends did know

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How it doth grieve me that thy head is here!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: My lord, cheer up your spirits; our foes are nigh,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And this soft courage makes your followers faint.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: You promised knighthood to our forward son.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Unsheathe your sword and dub him presently.—

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Edward, kneel down.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Edward Plantagenet, arise a knight;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And learn this lesson: draw thy sword in right.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: My gracious father, by your kingly leave,

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: I’ll draw it as apparent to the crown,

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: And in that quarrel use it to the death.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Why, that is spoken like a toward prince.
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Royal commanders, be in readiness;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: For with a band of thirty thousand men

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Comes Warwick, backing of the Duke of York,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And in the towns, as they do march along,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Proclaims him king, and many fly to him.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Darraign your battle, for they are at hand.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: I would your highness would depart the field.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: The Queen hath best success when you are absent.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ay, good my lord, and leave us to our fortune.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Why, that’s my fortune too; therefore I’ll stay.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Be it with resolution then to fight.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: My royal father, cheer these noble lords,

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: And hearten those that fight in your defence.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Unsheathe your sword, good father; cry “Saint George!”

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: March. Enter Edward, George, Richard, Warwick, Norfolk, Montague and

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Soldiers.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Now, perjured Henry, wilt thou kneel for grace

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And set thy diadem upon my head,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Or bide the mortal fortune of the field?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Go rate thy minions, proud insulting boy!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Becomes it thee to be thus bold in terms

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Before thy sovereign and thy lawful king?

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: I am his king, and he should bow his knee.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: I was adopted heir by his consent.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Since when, his oath is broke; for, as I hear,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: You that are king, though he do wear the crown,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Have caused him by new act of Parliament

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: To blot out me and put his own son in.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And reason too:

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Who should succeed the father but the son?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Are you there, butcher? O, I cannot speak!

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Ay, crook-back; here I stand, to answer thee,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Or any he, the proudest of thy sort.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: ’Twas you that killed young Rutland, was it not?

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Ay, and old York, and yet not satisfied.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For God’s sake, lords, give signal to the fight.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: What sayst thou, Henry, wilt thou yield the crown?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Why, how now, long-tongued Warwick, dare you speak?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: When you and I met at Saint Albans last,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Your legs did better service than your hands.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Then ’twas my turn to fly, and now ’tis thine.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: You said so much before, and yet you fled.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: ’Twas not your valour, Clifford, drove me thence.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: No, nor your manhood that durst make you stay.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Northumberland, I hold thee reverently.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Break off the parley; for scarce I can refrain

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The execution of my big-swoln heart

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Upon that Clifford, that cruel child-killer.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: I slew thy father; call’st thou him a child?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Ay, like a dastard and a treacherous coward,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: As thou didst kill our tender brother Rutland,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But ere sunset I’ll make thee curse the deed.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Have done with words, my lords, and hear me speak.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Defy them then, or else hold close thy lips.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I prithee, give no limits to my tongue.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I am a king, and privileged to speak.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: My liege, the wound that bred this meeting here

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Cannot be cured by words; therefore be still.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Then, executioner, unsheathe thy sword.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: By Him that made us all, I am resolved

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That Clifford’s manhood lies upon his tongue.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Say, Henry, shall I have my right, or no?

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: A thousand men have broke their fasts today

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: That ne’er shall dine unless thou yield the crown.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: If thou deny, their blood upon thy head;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For York in justice puts his armour on.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: If that be right which Warwick says is right,

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: There is no wrong, but everything is right.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Whoever got thee, there thy mother stands;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For well I wot thou hast thy mother’s tongue.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But thou art neither like thy sire nor dam,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But like a foul misshapen stigmatic,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Marked by the Destinies to be avoided,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: As venom toads or lizards’ dreadful stings.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Iron of Naples, hid with English gilt,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Whose father bears the title of a king,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: As if a channel should be called the sea,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Sham’st thou not, knowing whence thou art extraught,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To let thy tongue detect thy base-born heart?

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: A wisp of straw were worth a thousand crowns

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: To make this shameless callet know herself.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Helen of Greece was fairer far than thou,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Although thy husband may be Menelaus;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And ne’er was Agamemnon’s brother wronged

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: By that false woman as this king by thee.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: His father revelled in the heart of France,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And tamed the King, and made the Dauphin stoop;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And had he matched according to his state,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: He might have kept that glory to this day;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: But when he took a beggar to his bed

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And graced thy poor sire with his bridal day,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Even then that sunshine brewed a shower for him

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: That washed his father’s fortunes forth of France

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And heaped sedition on his crown at home.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: For what hath broached this tumult but thy pride?

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Hadst thou been meek, our title still had slept;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And we, in pity of the gentle king,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Had slipped our claim until another age.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: But when we saw our sunshine made thy spring,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: And that thy summer bred us no increase,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: We set the axe to thy usurping root;

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: And though the edge hath something hit ourselves,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Yet know thou, since we have begun to strike,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: We’ll never leave till we have hewn thee down

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Or bathed thy growing with our heated bloods.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And in this resolution I defy thee;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Not willing any longer conference,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Since thou deniest the gentle King to speak.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Sound trumpets! Let our bloody colours wave;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And either victory or else a grave!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Stay, Edward.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: No, wrangling woman, we’ll no longer stay.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: These words will cost ten thousand lives this day.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A field of battle between Towton and Saxton, in Yorkshire

lines.text: Alarums. Excursions. Enter Warwick.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Forspent with toil, as runners with a race,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I lay me down a little while to breathe;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For strokes received, and many blows repaid,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Have robbed my strong-knit sinews of their strength,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And spite of spite, needs must I rest awhile.
Enter Edward, running.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Smile, gentle heaven, or strike, ungentle death;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: For this world frowns and Edward’s sun is clouded.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: How now, my lord, what hap? What hope of good?
Enter George.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Our hap is loss, our hope but sad despair;

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Our ranks are broke and ruin follows us.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: What counsel give you? Whither shall we fly?

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Bootless is flight, they follow us with wings;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And weak we are and cannot shun pursuit.
Enter Richard.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Ah, Warwick, why hast thou withdrawn thyself?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Thy brother’s blood the thirsty earth hath drunk,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Broached with the steely point of Clifford’s lance;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And in the very pangs of death he cried,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Like to a dismal clangor heard from far,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: “Warwick, revenge! Brother, revenge my death!”

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: So, underneath the belly of their steeds,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That stained their fetlocks in his smoking blood,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The noble gentleman gave up the ghost.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Then let the earth be drunken with our blood;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I’ll kill my horse because I will not fly.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Why stand we like soft-hearted women here,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Wailing our losses whiles the foe doth rage,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And look upon, as if the tragedy

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Were played in jest by counterfeiting actors?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Here on my knee I vow to God above

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I’ll never pause again, never stand still,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Till either death hath closed these eyes of mine,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Or Fortune given me measure of revenge.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: O Warwick, I do bend my knee with thine,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And in this vow do chain my soul to thine!

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And, ere my knee rise from the earth’s cold face,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: I throw my hands, mine eyes, my heart to Thee,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Thou setter up and plucker down of kings,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Beseeching Thee, if with Thy will it stands

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: That to my foes this body must be prey,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Yet that Thy brazen gates of heaven may ope,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And give sweet passage to my sinful soul.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Now, lords, take leave until we meet again,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Where’er it be, in heaven or in earth.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Brother, give me thy hand; and, gentle Warwick,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Let me embrace thee in my weary arms.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I, that did never weep, now melt with woe

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That winter should cut off our spring-time so.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Away, away! Once more, sweet lords, farewell.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Yet let us all together to our troops,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: And give them leave to fly that will not stay,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: And call them pillars that will stand to us;

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: And if we thrive, promise them such rewards

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: As victors wear at the Olympian games.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: This may plant courage in their quailing breasts,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: For yet is hope of life and victory.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Forslow no longer; make we hence amain.
[_Exeunt._]
Excursions. Enter Richard and Clifford.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Now, Clifford, I have singled thee alone.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Suppose this arm is for the Duke of York,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And this for Rutland; both bound to revenge,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Wert thou environed with a brazen wall.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Now, Richard, I am with thee here alone.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: This is the hand that stabbed thy father York,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And this the hand that slew thy brother Rutland;

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And here’s the heart that triumphs in their death

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And cheers these hands that slew thy sire and brother

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: To execute the like upon thyself;

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And so have at thee!

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: They fight. Warwick comes; Clifford flies.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Nay, Warwick, single out some other chase;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For I myself will hunt this wolf to death.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter King Henry.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: This battle fares like to the morning’s war,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: When dying clouds contend with growing light,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What time the shepherd, blowing of his nails,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Can neither call it perfect day nor night.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Now sways it this way, like a mighty sea

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Forced by the tide to combat with the wind;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Now sways it that way, like the selfsame sea

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Forced to retire by fury of the wind.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Sometime the flood prevails, and then the wind;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Now one the better, then another best,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Both tugging to be victors, breast to breast,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Yet neither conqueror nor conquered.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So is the equal poise of this fell war.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Here on this molehill will I sit me down.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To whom God will, there be the victory!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For Margaret my queen, and Clifford too,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Have chid me from the battle, swearing both

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: They prosper best of all when I am thence.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Would I were dead, if God’s good will were so;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For what is in this world but grief and woe?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O God! Methinks it were a happy life

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To be no better than a homely swain;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To sit upon a hill, as I do now,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To carve out dials quaintly, point by point,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thereby to see the minutes how they run:

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How many make the hour full complete,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How many hours brings about the day,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How many days will finish up the year,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How many years a mortal man may live.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: When this is known, then to divide the times:

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So many hours must I tend my flock;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So many hours must I take my rest;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So many hours must I contemplate;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So many hours must I sport myself;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So many days my ewes have been with young;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So many weeks ere the poor fools will ean;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So many years ere I shall shear the fleece.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So minutes, hours, days, months, and years,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Passed over to the end they were created,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Would bring white hairs unto a quiet grave.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ah, what a life were this! How sweet, how lovely!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Gives not the hawthorn bush a sweeter shade

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To shepherds looking on their silly sheep

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Than doth a rich embroidered canopy

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To kings that fear their subjects’ treachery?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O, yes, it doth; a thousand-fold it doth.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And to conclude, the shepherd’s homely curds,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: His cold thin drink out of his leather bottle,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: His wonted sleep under a fresh tree’s shade,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: All which secure and sweetly he enjoys,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Is far beyond a prince’s delicates—

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: His viands sparkling in a golden cup,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: His body couched in a curious bed,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: When care, mistrust, and treason waits on him.
Alarum. Enter a Son that hath killed his father, bringing in the dead body.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: Ill blows the wind that profits nobody.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: This man, whom hand to hand I slew in fight,

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: May be possessed with some store of crowns;

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: And I, that haply take them from him now,

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: May yet ere night yield both my life and them

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: To some man else, as this dead man doth me.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: Who’s this? O God! It is my father’s face,

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: Whom in this conflict I unwares have killed.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: O heavy times, begetting such events!

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: From London by the King was I pressed forth;

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: My father, being the Earl of Warwick’s man,

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: Came on the part of York, pressed by his master;

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: And I, who at his hands received my life,

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: Have by my hands of life bereaved him.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: Pardon me, God, I knew not what I did;

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: And pardon, father, for I knew not thee.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: My tears shall wipe away these bloody marks,

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: And no more words till they have flowed their fill.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O piteous spectacle! O bloody times!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whiles lions war and battle for their dens,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Poor harmless lambs abide their enmity.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Weep, wretched man, I’ll aid thee tear for tear;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And let our hearts and eyes, like civil war,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Be blind with tears and break o’ercharged with grief.
Enter a Father who has killed his son, with the body in his arms.

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: Thou that so stoutly hath resisted me,

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: Give me thy gold, if thou hast any gold,

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: For I have bought it with an hundred blows.

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: But let me see: is this our foeman’s face?

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: Ah, no, no, no; it is mine only son!

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: Ah, boy, if any life be left in thee,

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: Throw up thine eye! See, see what showers arise,

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: Blown with the windy tempest of my heart

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: Upon thy wounds, that kill mine eye and heart!

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: O, pity, God, this miserable age!

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: What stratagems, how fell, how butcherly,

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: Erroneous, mutinous, and unnatural,

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: This deadly quarrel daily doth beget!

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: O boy, thy father gave thee life too soon,

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: And hath bereft thee of thy life too late!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Woe above woe, grief more than common grief!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O that my death would stay these ruthful deeds!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O pity, pity, gentle heaven, pity!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The red rose and the white are on his face,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The fatal colours of our striving houses;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The one his purple blood right well resembles,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The other his pale cheeks, methinks, presenteth.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Wither one rose, and let the other flourish!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If you contend, a thousand lives must wither.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: How will my mother for a father’s death

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: Take on with me and ne’er be satisfied!

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: How will my wife for slaughter of my son

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: Shed seas of tears and ne’er be satisfied!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How will the country for these woeful chances

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Misthink the King and not be satisfied!

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: Was ever son so rued a father’s death?

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: Was ever father so bemoaned his son?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Was ever king so grieved for subjects’ woe?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Much is your sorrow, mine ten times so much.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: I’ll bear thee hence, where I may weep my fill.
[_Exit with the body._]

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: These arms of mine shall be thy winding-sheet;

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: My heart, sweet boy, shall be thy sepulchre,

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: For from my heart thine image ne’er shall go.

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: My sighing breast shall be thy funeral bell;

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: And so obsequious will thy father be,

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: Even for the loss of thee, having no more,

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: As Priam was for all his valiant sons.

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: I’ll bear thee hence; and let them fight that will,

lines.speaker: FATHER
lines.text: For I have murdered where I should not kill.
[_Exit with the body._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Sad-hearted men, much overgone with care,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Here sits a king more woeful than you are.
Alarums. Excursions. Enter Queen Margaret, Prince of Wales and Exeter.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Fly, father, fly, for all your friends are fled,

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: And Warwick rages like a chafed bull.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Away, for death doth hold us in pursuit.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Mount you, my lord; towards Berwick post amain.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Edward and Richard, like a brace of greyhounds

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Having the fearful flying hare in sight,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: With fiery eyes sparkling for very wrath,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And bloody steel grasped in their ireful hands,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Are at our backs; and therefore hence amain.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Away, for vengeance comes along with them.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Nay, stay not to expostulate; make speed,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Or else come after; I’ll away before.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Nay, take me with thee, good sweet Exeter;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Not that I fear to stay, but love to go

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whither the Queen intends. Forward; away!
[_Exeunt._]
A loud alarum. Enter Clifford, wounded.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Here burns my candle out; ay, here it dies,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Which whiles it lasted gave King Henry light.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: O Lancaster, I fear thy overthrow

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: More than my body’s parting with my soul!

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: My love and fear glued many friends to thee;

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And, now I fall, thy tough commixtures melts,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Impairing Henry, strengthening misproud York.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: The common people swarm like summer flies;

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And whither fly the gnats but to the sun?

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And who shines now but Henry’s enemies?

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: O Phoebus, hadst thou never given consent

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: That Phaëthon should check thy fiery steeds,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Thy burning car never had scorched the earth!

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And, Henry, hadst thou swayed as kings should do,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Or as thy father and his father did,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Giving no ground unto the house of York,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: They never then had sprung like summer flies;

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: I, and ten thousand in this luckless realm

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Had left no mourning widows for our death,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And thou this day hadst kept thy chair in peace.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: For what doth cherish weeds but gentle air?

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And what makes robbers bold but too much lenity?

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Bootless are plaints, and cureless are my wounds;

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: No way to fly, nor strength to hold out flight.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: The foe is merciless and will not pity,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: For at their hands I have deserved no pity.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: The air hath got into my deadly wounds,

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: And much effuse of blood doth make me faint.

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: Come, York and Richard, Warwick, and the rest;

lines.speaker: CLIFFORD
lines.text: I stabbed your fathers’ bosoms, split my breast.
[_He faints._]
Alarum and retreat. Enter Edward, George, Richard, Montague, Warwick and Soldiers.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Now breathe we, lords. Good fortune bids us pause

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And smooth the frowns of war with peaceful looks.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Some troops pursue the bloody-minded Queen

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: That led calm Henry, though he were a king,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: As doth a sail, filled with a fretting gust,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Command an argosy to stem the waves.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: But think you, lords, that Clifford fled with them?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: No, ’tis impossible he should escape;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For, though before his face I speak the words,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Your brother Richard marked him for the grave,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And whereso’er he is, he’s surely dead.
[_Clifford groans and dies._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Whose soul is that which takes her heavy leave?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: A deadly groan, like life and death’s departing.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: See who it is; and, now the battle’s ended,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: If friend or foe, let him be gently used.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Revoke that doom of mercy, for ’tis Clifford,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Who, not contented that he lopped the branch

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: In hewing Rutland when his leaves put forth,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But set his murdering knife unto the root

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: From whence that tender spray did sweetly spring,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I mean our princely father, Duke of York.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: From off the gates of York fetch down the head,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Your father’s head, which Clifford placed there;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Instead whereof let this supply the room.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Measure for measure must be answered.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Bring forth that fatal screech-owl to our house,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: That nothing sung but death to us and ours;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Now death shall stop his dismal threatening sound,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And his ill-boding tongue no more shall speak.
[_Soldiers bring the body forward._]

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I think his understanding is bereft.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Speak, Clifford, dost thou know who speaks to thee?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Dark cloudy death o’ershades his beams of life,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And he nor sees nor hears us, what we say.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: O, would he did, and so, perhaps, he doth!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: ’Tis but his policy to counterfeit,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Because he would avoid such bitter taunts

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Which in the time of death he gave our father.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: If so thou think’st, vex him with eager words.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Clifford, ask mercy, and obtain no grace.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Clifford, repent in bootless penitence.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Clifford, devise excuses for thy faults.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: While we devise fell tortures for thy faults.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Thou didst love York, and I am son to York.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Thou pitied’st Rutland, I will pity thee.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Where’s Captain Margaret to fence you now?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: They mock thee, Clifford; swear as thou wast wont.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: What, not an oath? Nay then, the world goes hard

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: When Clifford cannot spare his friends an oath.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I know by that he’s dead; and, by my soul,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: If this right hand would buy but two hours’ life,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That I in all despite might rail at him,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: This hand should chop it off, and with the issuing blood

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Stifle the villain whose unstaunched thirst

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: York and young Rutland could not satisfy.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Ay, but he’s dead. Off with the traitor’s head,
