lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And rear it in the place your father’s stands.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And now to London with triumphant march,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: There to be crowned England’s royal king;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: From whence shall Warwick cut the sea to France,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And ask the Lady Bona for thy queen.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: So shalt thou sinew both these lands together,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And, having France thy friend, thou shalt not dread

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: The scattered foe that hopes to rise again;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For though they cannot greatly sting to hurt,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Yet look to have them buzz to offend thine ears.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: First will I see the coronation,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And then to Brittany I’ll cross the sea

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: To effect this marriage, so it please my lord.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Even as thou wilt, sweet Warwick, let it be;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: For in thy shoulder do I build my seat,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And never will I undertake the thing

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Wherein thy counsel and consent is wanting.

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Richard, I will create thee Duke of Gloucester;

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: And George, of Clarence. Warwick, as ourself,

lines.speaker: EDWARD
lines.text: Shall do and undo as him pleaseth best.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Let me be Duke of Clarence, George of Gloucester,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For Gloucester’s dukedom is too ominous.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Tut, that’s a foolish observation.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Richard, be Duke of Gloucester. Now to London,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: To see these honours in possession.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A Forest in the North of England

lines.text: Enter two Keepers with crossbows in their hands.
1 KEEPER. Under this thick-grown brake we’ll shroud ourselves, For through this laund anon the deer will come; And in this covert will we make our stand, Culling the principal of all the deer.
2 KEEPER. I’ll stay above the hill, so both may shoot.

1 KEEPER. That cannot be; the noise of thy crossbow Will scare the herd, and so my shoot is lost. Here stand we both, and aim we at the best; And, for the time shall not seem tedious, I’ll tell thee what befell me on a day In this self place where now we mean to stand.
2 KEEPER. Here comes a man; let’s stay till he be past.
Enter King Henry, disguised, with a prayer-book.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: From Scotland am I stolen, even of pure love,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To greet mine own land with my wishful sight.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No, Harry, Harry, ’tis no land of thine;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thy place is filled, thy sceptre wrung from thee,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thy balm washed off wherewith thou wast anointed.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No bending knee will call thee Caesar now,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No humble suitors press to speak for right,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No, not a man comes for redress of thee;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For how can I help them and not myself?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: 1 KEEPER.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ay, here’s a deer whose skin’s a keeper’s fee.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: This is the quondam king; let’s seize upon him.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Let me embrace thee, sour adversity,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For wise men say it is the wisest course.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: 2 KEEPER.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Why linger we? Let us lay hands upon him.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: 1 KEEPER.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Forbear awhile; we’ll hear a little more.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My queen and son are gone to France for aid;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And, as I hear, the great commanding Warwick

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Is thither gone to crave the French King’s sister

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To wife for Edward. If this news be true,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Poor queen and son, your labour is but lost,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For Warwick is a subtle orator,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And Lewis a prince soon won with moving words.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: By this account, then, Margaret may win him,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For she’s a woman to be pitied much.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Her sighs will make a batt’ry in his breast,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Her tears will pierce into a marble heart;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The tiger will be mild whiles she doth mourn,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And Nero will be tainted with remorse

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To hear and see her plaints, her brinish tears.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ay, but she’s come to beg, Warwick to give;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: She on his left side craving aid for Henry;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: He on his right asking a wife for Edward.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: She weeps and says her Henry is deposed;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: He smiles and says his Edward is installed;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That she, poor wretch, for grief can speak no more;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whiles Warwick tells his title, smooths the wrong,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Inferreth arguments of mighty strength,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And in conclusion wins the King from her

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: With promise of his sister, and what else,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To strengthen and support King Edward’s place.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O Margaret, thus ’twill be; and thou, poor soul,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Art then forsaken, as thou went’st forlorn.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: 2 KEEPER.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Say, what art thou, that talk’st of kings and queens?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: More than I seem, and less than I was born to:

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: A man at least, for less I should not be;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And men may talk of kings, and why not I?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: 2 KEEPER.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ay, but thou talk’st as if thou wert a king.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Why, so I am, in mind; and that’s enough.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: 2 KEEPER.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But, if thou be a king, where is thy crown?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My crown is in my heart, not on my head;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Not decked with diamonds and Indian stones,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Not to be seen. My crown is called content;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: A crown it is that seldom kings enjoy.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: 2 KEEPER.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Well, if you be a king crowned with content,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Your crown content and you must be contented

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To go along with us; for, as we think,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: You are the king King Edward hath deposed;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And we his subjects, sworn in all allegiance,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Will apprehend you as his enemy.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But did you never swear, and break an oath?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: 2 KEEPER.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No, never such an oath; nor will not now.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Where did you dwell when I was King of England?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: 2 KEEPER.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Here in this country, where we now remain.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I was anointed king at nine months old;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My father and my grandfather were kings,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And you were sworn true subjects unto me.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And tell me, then, have you not broke your oaths?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: 1 KEEPER.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No, for we were subjects but while you were king.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Why, am I dead? Do I not breathe a man?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ah, simple men, you know not what you swear.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Look, as I blow this feather from my face,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And as the air blows it to me again,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Obeying with my wind when I do blow,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And yielding to another when it blows,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Commanded always by the greater gust,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Such is the lightness of you common men.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But do not break your oaths; for of that sin

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My mild entreaty shall not make you guilty.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Go where you will, the King shall be commanded;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And be you kings; command, and I’ll obey.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: 1 KEEPER.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We are true subjects to the King, King Edward.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So would you be again to Henry

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If he were seated as King Edward is.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: 1 KEEPER.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We charge you, in God’s name and the King’s

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To go with us unto the officers.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: In God’s name, lead; your king’s name be obeyed,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And what God will, that let your king perform;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And what he will, I humbly yield unto.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter King Edward, Richard (Duke of Gloucester), George (Duke of Clarence) and Lady Grey.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Brother of Gloucester, at Saint Albans field

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: This lady’s husband, Sir John Grey, was slain,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: His land then seized on by the conqueror.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Her suit is now to repossess those lands,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Which we in justice cannot well deny,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Because in quarrel of the house of York

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: The worthy gentleman did lose his life.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Your Highness shall do well to grant her suit;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: It were dishonour to deny it her.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: It were no less; but yet I’ll make a pause.
[_Aside to George_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Yea, is it so?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I see the lady hath a thing to grant

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Before the King will grant her humble suit.
[_Aside to Richard_.]

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: He knows the game; how true he keeps the wind!
[_Aside to George_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Silence!

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Widow, we will consider of your suit,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And come some other time to know our mind.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: Right gracious lord, I cannot brook delay.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: May it please your Highness to resolve me now,

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: And what your pleasure is shall satisfy me.
[_Aside to George_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Ay, widow? Then I’ll warrant you all your lands,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: An if what pleases him shall pleasure you.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Fight closer, or, good faith, you’ll catch a blow.
[_Aside to Richard_.]

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: I fear her not, unless she chance to fall.
[_Aside to George_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: God forbid that, for he’ll take vantages.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: How many children hast thou, widow? Tell me.
[_Aside to Richard_.]

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: I think he means to beg a child of her.
[_Aside to George_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Nay, whip me then; he’ll rather give her two.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: Three, my most gracious lord.
[_Aside to George_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: You shall have four if you’ll be ruled by him.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: ’Twere pity they should lose their father’s lands.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: Be pitiful, dread lord, and grant it then.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Lords, give us leave; I’ll try this widow’s wit.
[_Aside to George_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Ay, good leave have you; for you will have leave

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Till youth take leave and leave you to the crutch.
[_Richard and George stand aside._]

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Now tell me, madam, do you love your children?

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: Ay, full as dearly as I love myself.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And would you not do much to do them good?

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: To do them good I would sustain some harm.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Then get your husband’s lands to do them good.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: Therefore I came unto your majesty.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: I’ll tell you how these lands are to be got.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: So shall you bind me to your Highness’ service.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: What service wilt thou do me if I give them?

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: What you command that rests in me to do.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: But you will take exceptions to my boon.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: No, gracious lord, except I cannot do it.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Ay, but thou canst do what I mean to ask.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: Why, then, I will do what your Grace commands.
[_Aside to George_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: He plies her hard; and much rain wears the marble.
[_Aside to Richard_.]

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: As red as fire! Nay, then her wax must melt.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: Why stops my lord? Shall I not hear my task?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: An easy task; ’tis but to love a king.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: That’s soon performed, because I am a subject.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Why, then, thy husband’s lands I freely give thee.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: I take my leave with many thousand thanks.
[_Aside to George_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The match is made; she seals it with a curtsy.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: But stay thee; ’tis the fruits of love I mean.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: The fruits of love I mean, my loving liege.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Ay, but, I fear me, in another sense.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: What love, thinkst thou, I sue so much to get?

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: My love till death, my humble thanks, my prayers;

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: That love which virtue begs, and virtue grants.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: No, by my troth, I did not mean such love.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: Why, then, you mean not as I thought you did.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: But now you partly may perceive my mind.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: My mind will never grant what I perceive

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: Your Highness aims at, if I aim aright.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: To tell thee plain, I aim to lie with thee.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: To tell you plain, I had rather lie in prison.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Why, then thou shalt not have thy husband’s lands.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: Why, then mine honesty shall be my dower,

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: For by that loss I will not purchase them.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Therein thou wrong’st thy children mightily.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: Herein your Highness wrongs both them and me.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: But, mighty lord, this merry inclination

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: Accords not with the sadness of my suit.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: Please you dismiss me either with ay or no.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Ay, if thou wilt say ay to my request;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: No, if thou dost say no to my demand.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: Then no, my lord. My suit is at an end.
[_Aside to George_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The widow likes him not, she knits her brows.
[_Aside to Richard_.]

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: He is the bluntest wooer in Christendom.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Her looks doth argue her replete with modesty;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Her words doth show her wit incomparable;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: All her perfections challenge sovereignty.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: One way or other, she is for a king,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And she shall be my love, or else my queen.—

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Say that King Edward take thee for his queen?

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: ’Tis better said than done, my gracious lord.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: I am a subject fit to jest withal,

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: But far unfit to be a sovereign.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Sweet widow, by my state I swear to thee,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: I speak no more than what my soul intends;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And that is to enjoy thee for my love.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: And that is more than I will yield unto.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: I know I am too mean to be your queen,

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: And yet too good to be your concubine.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: You cavil, widow; I did mean my queen.

lines.speaker: LADY GREY
lines.text: ’Twill grieve your Grace my sons should call you father.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: No more than when my daughters call thee mother.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Thou art a widow, and thou hast some children;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And, by God’s mother, I, being but a bachelor,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Have other some. Why, ’tis a happy thing

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: To be the father unto many sons.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Answer no more, for thou shalt be my queen.
[_Aside to George_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The ghostly father now hath done his shrift.
[_Aside to Richard_.]

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: When he was made a shriver, ’twas for shift.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Brothers, you muse what chat we two have had.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Richard and George come forward.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The widow likes it not, for she looks very sad.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: You’d think it strange if I should marry her.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: To whom, my lord?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Why, Clarence, to myself.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That would be ten days’ wonder at the least.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: That’s a day longer than a wonder lasts.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: By so much is the wonder in extremes.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Well, jest on, brothers. I can tell you both

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Her suit is granted for her husband’s lands.
Enter a Nobleman.

lines.speaker: NOBLEMAN
lines.text: My gracious lord, Henry your foe is taken,

lines.speaker: NOBLEMAN
lines.text: And brought your prisoner to your palace gate.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: See that he be conveyed unto the Tower.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And go we, brothers, to the man that took him,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: To question of his apprehension.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Widow, go you along. Lords, use her honourably.
[_Exeunt all but Richard._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Ay, Edward will use women honourably.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Would he were wasted, marrow, bones, and all,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That from his loins no hopeful branch may spring,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To cross me from the golden time I look for!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And yet, between my soul’s desire and me—

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The lustful Edward’s title buried—

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Is Clarence, Henry, and his son young Edward,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And all the unlooked-for issue of their bodies,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To take their rooms ere I can place myself.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: A cold premeditation for my purpose!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Why then I do but dream on sovereignty;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Like one that stands upon a promontory

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And spies a far-off shore where he would tread,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Wishing his foot were equal with his eye,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And chides the sea that sunders him from thence,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Saying he’ll lade it dry to have his way.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: So do I wish the crown, being so far off,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And so I chide the means that keeps me from it;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And so I say I’ll cut the causes off,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Flattering me with impossibilities.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: My eye’s too quick, my heart o’erweens too much,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Unless my hand and strength could equal them.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Well, say there is no kingdom then for Richard,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: What other pleasure can the world afford?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I’ll make my heaven in a lady’s lap,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And deck my body in gay ornaments,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And ’witch sweet ladies with my words and looks.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: O miserable thought, and more unlikely

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Than to accomplish twenty golden crowns.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Why, Love forswore me in my mother’s womb,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And, for I should not deal in her soft laws,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: She did corrupt frail Nature with some bribe

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To shrink mine arm up like a withered shrub;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To make an envious mountain on my back,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Where sits Deformity to mock my body;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To shape my legs of an unequal size;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To disproportion me in every part,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Like to a chaos, or an unlicked bear-whelp

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That carries no impression like the dam.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And am I then a man to be beloved?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: O monstrous fault to harbour such a thought!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Then, since this earth affords no joy to me

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But to command, to check, to o’erbear such

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: As are of better person than myself,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I’ll make my heaven to dream upon the crown,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And, whiles I live, t’ account this world but hell

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Until my misshaped trunk that bear this head

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Be round impaled with a glorious crown.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And yet I know not how to get the crown,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For many lives stand between me and home;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And I, like one lost in a thorny wood,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That rents the thorns, and is rent with the thorns,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Seeking a way, and straying from the way,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Not knowing how to find the open air,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But toiling desperately to find it out,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Torment myself to catch the English crown.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And from that torment I will free myself,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Or hew my way out with a bloody axe.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Why, I can smile, and murder while I smile,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And cry “Content!” to that which grieves my heart,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And wet my cheeks with artificial tears,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And frame my face to all occasions.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I’ll drown more sailors than the mermaid shall,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I’ll slay more gazers than the basilisk;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I’ll play the orator as well as Nestor,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Deceive more slyly than Ulysses could,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And, like a Sinon, take another Troy.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I can add colours to the chameleon,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Change shapes with Proteus for advantages,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And set the murderous Machiavel to school.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Can I do this, and cannot get a crown?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Tut, were it farther off, I’ll pluck it down.
[_Exit._]
Flourish. Enter Lewis, the French King, his sister the Lady Bona, his Admiral called Bourbon, Prince Edward, Queen Margaret, and the Earl of Oxford. Lewis sits, and riseth up again.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Fair Queen of England, worthy Margaret,

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Sit down with us. It ill befits thy state

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: And birth that thou shouldst stand while Lewis doth sit.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: No, mighty King of France. Now Margaret

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Must strike her sail and learn awhile to serve

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Where kings command. I was, I must confess,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Great Albion’s queen in former golden days;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But now mischance hath trod my title down

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And with dishonour laid me on the ground,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Where I must take like seat unto my fortune

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And to my humble seat conform myself.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Why, say, fair queen, whence springs this deep despair?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: From such a cause as fills mine eyes with tears

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And stops my tongue, while heart is drowned in cares.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Whate’er it be, be thou still like thyself,

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: And sit thee by our side. Yield not thy neck
[_Seats her by him._]

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: To Fortune’s yoke, but let thy dauntless mind

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Still ride in triumph over all mischance.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Be plain, Queen Margaret, and tell thy grief;

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: It shall be eased if France can yield relief.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Those gracious words revive my drooping thoughts

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And give my tongue-tied sorrows leave to speak.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Now, therefore, be it known to noble Lewis

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: That Henry, sole possessor of my love,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Is, of a king, become a banished man

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And forced to live in Scotland a forlorn;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: While proud ambitious Edward, Duke of York,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Usurps the regal title and the seat

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Of England’s true-anointed lawful king.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: This is the cause that I, poor Margaret,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: With this my son, Prince Edward, Henry’s heir,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Am come to crave thy just and lawful aid;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And if thou fail us, all our hope is done.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Scotland hath will to help, but cannot help;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Our people and our peers are both misled,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Our treasure seized, our soldiers put to flight,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And, as thou seest, ourselves in heavy plight.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Renowned queen, with patience calm the storm

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: While we bethink a means to break it off.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The more we stay, the stronger grows our foe.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: The more I stay, the more I’ll succour thee.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: O, but impatience waiteth on true sorrow.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And see where comes the breeder of my sorrow.
Enter Warwick.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: What’s he approacheth boldly to our presence?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Our Earl of Warwick, Edward’s greatest friend.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Welcome, brave Warwick. What brings thee to France?
[_He descends. Queen Margaret rises._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ay, now begins a second storm to rise,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: For this is he that moves both wind and tide.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: From worthy Edward, king of Albion,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: My lord and sovereign, and thy vowed friend,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I come, in kindness and unfeigned love,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: First, to do greetings to thy royal person,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And then to crave a league of amity,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And lastly, to confirm that amity

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: With nuptial knot, if thou vouchsafe to grant

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That virtuous Lady Bona, thy fair sister,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: To England’s king in lawful marriage.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: If that go forward, Henry’s hope is done.
[_To Bona_.]

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And, gracious madam, in our king’s behalf,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I am commanded, with your leave and favour,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Humbly to kiss your hand, and with my tongue

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: To tell the passion of my sovereign’s heart,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Where fame, late entering at his heedful ears,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Hath placed thy beauty’s image and thy virtue.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: King Lewis and Lady Bona, hear me speak

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Before you answer Warwick. His demand

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Springs not from Edward’s well-meant honest love,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But from deceit, bred by necessity;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: For how can tyrants safely govern home

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Unless abroad they purchase great alliance?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: To prove him tyrant this reason may suffice,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: That Henry liveth still; but were he dead,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Yet here Prince Edward stands, King Henry’s son.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Look therefore, Lewis, that by this league and marriage

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thou draw not on thy danger and dishonour;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: For though usurpers sway the rule awhile,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Yet heavens are just, and time suppresseth wrongs.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Injurious Margaret!

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: And why not Queen?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Because thy father Henry did usurp,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And thou no more art prince than she is queen.

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Then Warwick disannuls great John of Gaunt,

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Which did subdue the greatest part of Spain;

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: And after John of Gaunt, Henry the Fourth,

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Whose wisdom was a mirror to the wisest;

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: And after that wise prince, Henry the Fifth,

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Who by his prowess conquered all France.

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: From these our Henry lineally descends.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Oxford, how haps it in this smooth discourse

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: You told not how Henry the Sixth hath lost

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: All that which Henry the Fifth had gotten?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Methinks these peers of France should smile at that.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But for the rest: you tell a pedigree

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Of threescore and two years, a silly time

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: To make prescription for a kingdom’s worth.

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Why, Warwick, canst thou speak against thy liege,

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Whom thou obeyed’st thirty and six years,

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: And not bewray thy treason with a blush?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Can Oxford, that did ever fence the right,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Now buckler falsehood with a pedigree?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For shame! Leave Henry, and call Edward king.

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Call him my king by whose injurious doom

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: My elder brother, the Lord Aubrey Vere,

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Was done to death? And more than so, my father,

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Even in the downfall of his mellowed years,

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: When nature brought him to the door of death?

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: No, Warwick, no; while life upholds this arm,

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: This arm upholds the house of Lancaster.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And I the house of York.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Queen Margaret, Prince Edward, and Oxford,

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Vouchsafe at our request to stand aside

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: While I use further conference with Warwick.
[_They stand aloof._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Heavens grant that Warwick’s words bewitch him not!

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Now, Warwick, tell me, even upon thy conscience,

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Is Edward your true king? For I were loath

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: To link with him that were not lawful chosen.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Thereon I pawn my credit and mine honour.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: But is he gracious in the people’s eye?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: The more that Henry was unfortunate.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Then further, all dissembling set aside,

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Tell me for truth the measure of his love

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Unto our sister Bona.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Such it seems

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: As may beseem a monarch like himself.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Myself have often heard him say and swear

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That this his love was an eternal plant,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Whereof the root was fixed in virtue’s ground,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: The leaves and fruit maintained with beauty’s sun,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Exempt from envy, but not from disdain,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Unless the Lady Bona quit his pain.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Now, sister, let us hear your firm resolve.

lines.speaker: BONA
lines.text: Your grant or your denial shall be mine.
[_To Warwick_]

lines.speaker: BONA
lines.text: Yet I confess that often ere this day,

lines.speaker: BONA
lines.text: When I have heard your king’s desert recounted,

lines.speaker: BONA
lines.text: Mine ear hath tempted judgment to desire.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Then, Warwick, thus: our sister shall be Edward’s.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: And now forthwith shall articles be drawn

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Touching the jointure that your king must make,

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Which with her dowry shall be counterpoised.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Draw near, Queen Margaret, and be a witness

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: That Bona shall be wife to the English king.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: To Edward, but not to the English king.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Deceitful Warwick, it was thy device

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: By this alliance to make void my suit.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Before thy coming Lewis was Henry’s friend.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: And still is friend to him and Margaret.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: But if your title to the crown be weak,

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: As may appear by Edward’s good success,

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Then ’tis but reason that I be released

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: From giving aid which late I promised.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Yet shall you have all kindness at my hand

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: That your estate requires and mine can yield.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Henry now lives in Scotland, at his ease,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Where, having nothing, nothing can he lose.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And as for you yourself, our quondam queen,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: You have a father able to maintain you,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And better ’twere you troubled him than France.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Peace, impudent and shameless Warwick,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Proud setter up and puller down of kings!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I will not hence till with my talk and tears,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Both full of truth, I make King Lewis behold

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thy sly conveyance and thy lord’s false love;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: For both of you are birds of selfsame feather.
[_Post blowing a horn within._]

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Warwick, this is some post to us or thee.
Enter the Post.

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: My lord ambassador, these letters are for you.

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: Sent from your brother, Marquess Montague.

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: These from our king unto your Majesty.

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: And, madam, these for you, from whom I know not.
[_They all read their letters._]

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: I like it well that our fair Queen and mistress

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Smiles at her news while Warwick frowns at his.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Nay, mark how Lewis stamps as he were nettled.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: I hope all’s for the best.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Warwick, what are thy news? And yours, fair Queen?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Mine, such as fill my heart with unhoped joys.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Mine, full of sorrow and heart’s discontent.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: What, has your king married the Lady Grey,

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: And now, to soothe your forgery and his,

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Sends me a paper to persuade me patience?

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Is this th’ alliance that he seeks with France?

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Dare he presume to scorn us in this manner?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I told your majesty as much before;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: This proveth Edward’s love and Warwick’s honesty.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: King Lewis, I here protest in sight of heaven,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And by the hope I have of heavenly bliss,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That I am clear from this misdeed of Edward’s—

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: No more my king, for he dishonours me,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But most himself, if he could see his shame.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Did I forget that by the house of York

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: My father came untimely to his death?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Did I let pass th’ abuse done to my niece?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Did I impale him with the regal crown?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Did I put Henry from his native right?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And am I guerdoned at the last with shame?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Shame on himself, for my desert is honour;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And to repair my honour lost for him,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I here renounce him and return to Henry.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: My noble Queen, let former grudges pass,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And henceforth I am thy true servitor.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I will revenge his wrong to Lady Bona,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And replant Henry in his former state.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Warwick, these words have turned my hate to love;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And I forgive and quite forget old faults,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And joy that thou becom’st King Henry’s friend.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: So much his friend, ay, his unfeigned friend,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That if King Lewis vouchsafe to furnish us

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: With some few bands of chosen soldiers,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I’ll undertake to land them on our coast

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And force the tyrant from his seat by war.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: ’Tis not his new-made bride shall succour him;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And as for Clarence, as my letters tell me,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: He’s very likely now to fall from him

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For matching more for wanton lust than honour,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Or than for strength and safety of our country.

lines.speaker: BONA
lines.text: Dear brother, how shall Bona be revenged

lines.speaker: BONA
lines.text: But by thy help to this distressed queen?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Renowned prince, how shall poor Henry live

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Unless thou rescue him from foul despair?

lines.speaker: BONA
lines.text: My quarrel and this English queen’s are one.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And mine, fair Lady Bona, joins with yours.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: And mine with hers, and thine, and Margaret’s.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Therefore, at last I firmly am resolved

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: You shall have aid.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Let me give humble thanks for all at once.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Then, England’s messenger, return in post

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: And tell false Edward, thy supposed king,

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: That Lewis of France is sending over maskers

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: To revel it with him and his new bride.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Thou seest what’s past; go fear thy king withal.

lines.speaker: BONA
lines.text: Tell him, in hope he’ll prove a widower shortly,

lines.speaker: BONA
lines.text: I’ll wear the willow garland for his sake.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Tell him my mourning weeds are laid aside,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And I am ready to put armour on.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Tell him from me that he hath done me wrong,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And therefore I’ll uncrown him ere ’t be long.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: There’s thy reward; be gone.
[_Exit Post._]

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: But, Warwick,

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Thou and Oxford, with five thousand men,

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Shall cross the seas and bid false Edward battle;

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: And, as occasion serves, this noble Queen

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: And prince shall follow with a fresh supply.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Yet, ere thou go, but answer me one doubt:

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: What pledge have we of thy firm loyalty?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: This shall assure my constant loyalty:

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That if our Queen and this young prince agree,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I’ll join mine eldest daughter and my joy

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: To him forthwith in holy wedlock bands.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Yes, I agree, and thank you for your motion.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Son Edward, she is fair and virtuous,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Therefore delay not, give thy hand to Warwick,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And with thy hand thy faith irrevocable

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: That only Warwick’s daughter shall be thine.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Yes, I accept her, for she well deserves it;

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: And here, to pledge my vow, I give my hand.
[_He gives his hand to Warwick._]

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Why stay we now? These soldiers shall be levied,

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: And thou, Lord Bourbon, our High Admiral,

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: Shall waft them over with our royal fleet.

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: I long till Edward fall by war’s mischance

lines.speaker: KING LEWIS
lines.text: For mocking marriage with a dame of France.
[_Exeunt all but Warwick._]

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I came from Edward as ambassador,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But I return his sworn and mortal foe.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Matter of marriage was the charge he gave me,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But dreadful war shall answer his demand.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Had he none else to make a stale but me?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Then none but I shall turn his jest to sorrow.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I was the chief that raised him to the crown,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And I’ll be chief to bring him down again:

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Not that I pity Henry’s misery,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But seek revenge on Edward’s mockery.
[_Exit._]
Enter Richard (Duke of Gloucester), George (Duke of Clarence), Somerset and Montague.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Now tell me, brother Clarence, what think you

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Of this new marriage with the Lady Grey?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Hath not our brother made a worthy choice?

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Alas, you know ’tis far from hence to France!

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: How could he stay till Warwick made return?

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: My lords, forbear this talk; here comes the King.
Flourish. Enter King Edward, attended; Lady Grey as Queen Elizabeth; Pembroke, Stafford, Hastings and others. Four stand on one side, and four on the other.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And his well-chosen bride.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: I mind to tell him plainly what I think.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Now, brother of Clarence, how like you our choice,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: That you stand pensive as half malcontent?

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: As well as Lewis of France or the Earl of Warwick,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Which are so weak of courage and in judgment

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: That they’ll take no offence at our abuse.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Suppose they take offence without a cause,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: They are but Lewis and Warwick; I am Edward,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Your King and Warwick’s, and must have my will.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And shall have your will, because our King.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Yet hasty marriage seldom proveth well.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Yea, brother Richard, are you offended too?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Not I.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: No, God forbid that I should wish them severed

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Whom God hath joined together. Ay, and ’twere pity

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To sunder them that yoke so well together.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Setting your scorns and your mislike aside,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Tell me some reason why the Lady Grey

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Should not become my wife and England’s queen.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And you too, Somerset and Montague,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Speak freely what you think.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Then this is mine opinion: that King Lewis

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Becomes your enemy for mocking him

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: About the marriage of the Lady Bona.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And Warwick, doing what you gave in charge,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Is now dishonoured by this new marriage.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: What if both Lewis and Warwick be appeased

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: By such invention as I can devise?

lines.speaker: MONTAGUE
lines.text: Yet to have joined with France in such alliance

lines.speaker: MONTAGUE
lines.text: Would more have strengthened this our commonwealth

lines.speaker: MONTAGUE
lines.text: ’Gainst foreign storms than any home-bred marriage.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Why, knows not Montague that of itself

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: England is safe, if true within itself?

lines.speaker: MONTAGUE
lines.text: But the safer when ’tis backed with France.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: ’Tis better using France than trusting France.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Let us be backed with God and with the seas

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Which He hath giv’n for fence impregnable,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And with their helps only defend ourselves.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: In them and in ourselves our safety lies.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: For this one speech Lord Hastings well deserves

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: To have the heir of the Lord Hungerford.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Ay, what of that? It was my will and grant;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And for this once my will shall stand for law.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And yet, methinks, your Grace hath not done well

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To give the heir and daughter of Lord Scales

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Unto the brother of your loving bride.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: She better would have fitted me or Clarence;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But in your bride you bury brotherhood.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Or else you would not have bestowed the heir

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Of the Lord Bonville on your new wife’s son,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: And leave your brothers to go speed elsewhere.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Alas, poor Clarence, is it for a wife

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: That thou art malcontent? I will provide thee.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: In choosing for yourself you showed your judgment,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Which being shallow, you shall give me leave

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: To play the broker in mine own behalf;

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: And to that end I shortly mind to leave you.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Leave me or tarry, Edward will be king,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And not be tied unto his brother’s will.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: My lords, before it pleased his Majesty

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: To raise my state to title of a queen,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Do me but right, and you must all confess

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: That I was not ignoble of descent,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: And meaner than myself have had like fortune.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: But as this title honours me and mine,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: So your dislikes, to whom I would be pleasing,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Doth cloud my joys with danger and with sorrow.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: My love, forbear to fawn upon their frowns.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: What danger or what sorrow can befall thee

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: So long as Edward is thy constant friend

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And their true sovereign, whom they must obey?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Nay, whom they shall obey, and love thee too,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Unless they seek for hatred at my hands;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Which if they do, yet will I keep thee safe,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And they shall feel the vengeance of my wrath.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I hear, yet say not much, but think the more.
Enter a Post.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Now, messenger, what letters or what news

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: From France?

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: My sovereign liege, no letters, and few words,

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: But such as I, without your special pardon,

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: Dare not relate.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Go to, we pardon thee. Therefore, in brief,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Tell me their words as near as thou canst guess them.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: What answer makes King Lewis unto our letters?

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: At my depart these were his very words:

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: “Go tell false Edward, thy supposed king,

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: That Lewis of France is sending over maskers

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: To revel it with him and his new bride.”

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Is Lewis so brave? Belike he thinks me Henry.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: But what said Lady Bona to my marriage?

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: These were her words, uttered with mild disdain:

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: “Tell him, in hope he’ll prove a widower shortly,

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: I’ll wear the willow garland for his sake.”

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: I blame not her; she could say little less;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: She had the wrong. But what said Henry’s queen?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: For I have heard that she was there in place.

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: “Tell him,” quoth she “my mourning weeds are done,

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: And I am ready to put armour on.”

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Belike she minds to play the Amazon.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: But what said Warwick to these injuries?

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: He, more incensed against your Majesty

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: Than all the rest, discharged me with these words:

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: “Tell him from me that he hath done me wrong,

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: And therefore I’ll uncrown him ere ’t be long.”

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Ha! Durst the traitor breathe out so proud words?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Well, I will arm me, being thus forewarned.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: They shall have wars and pay for their presumption.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: But say, is Warwick friends with Margaret?

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: Ay, gracious sovereign, they are so linked in friendship

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: That young Prince Edward marries Warwick’s daughter.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Belike the elder; Clarence will have the younger.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Now, brother king, farewell, and sit you fast,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: For I will hence to Warwick’s other daughter;

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: That, though I want a kingdom, yet in marriage

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: I may not prove inferior to yourself.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: You that love me and Warwick, follow me.
[_Exit George and Somerset follows._]
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Not I. My thoughts aim at a further matter;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I stay not for the love of Edward, but the crown.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Clarence and Somerset both gone to Warwick!

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Yet am I armed against the worst can happen,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And haste is needful in this desperate case.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Pembroke and Stafford, you in our behalf

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Go levy men and make prepare for war;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: They are already, or quickly will be, landed.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Myself in person will straight follow you.
[_Exeunt Pembroke and Stafford._]

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: But, ere I go, Hastings and Montague,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Resolve my doubt. You twain, of all the rest,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Are near to Warwick by blood and by alliance.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Tell me if you love Warwick more than me.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: If it be so, then both depart to him.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: I rather wish you foes than hollow friends.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: But if you mind to hold your true obedience,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Give me assurance with some friendly vow,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: That I may never have you in suspect.

lines.speaker: MONTAGUE
lines.text: So God help Montague as he proves true!

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And Hastings as he favours Edward’s cause!

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Now, brother Richard, will you stand by us?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Ay, in despite of all that shall withstand you.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Why, so! Then am I sure of victory.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Now, therefore, let us hence, and lose no hour

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Till we meet Warwick with his foreign power.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Warwick and Oxford in England, with French Soldiers.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Trust me, my lord, all hitherto goes well;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: The common people by numbers swarm to us.
Enter George (Duke of Clarence) and Somerset.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But see where Somerset and Clarence comes.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Speak suddenly, my lords: are we all friends?

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Fear not that, my lord.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Then, gentle Clarence, welcome unto Warwick;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And welcome, Somerset. I hold it cowardice

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: To rest mistrustful where a noble heart

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Hath pawned an open hand in sign of love;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Else might I think that Clarence, Edward’s brother,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Were but a feigned friend to our proceedings.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But welcome, sweet Clarence; my daughter shall be thine.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And now what rests but, in night’s coverture,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Thy brother being carelessly encamped,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: His soldiers lurking in the towns about,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And but attended by a simple guard,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: We may surprise and take him at our pleasure?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Our scouts have found the adventure very easy;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That, as Ulysses and stout Diomede

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: With sleight and manhood stole to Rhesus’ tents,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And brought from thence the Thracian fatal steeds,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: So we, well covered with the night’s black mantle,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: At unawares may beat down Edward’s guard,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And seize himself. I say not, slaughter him,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For I intend but only to surprise him.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: You that will follow me to this attempt,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Applaud the name of Henry with your leader.
[_They all cry “Henry!”_]

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Why then, let’s on our way in silent sort,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For Warwick and his friends, God and Saint George!
[_Exeunt._]
Enter three Watchmen to guard the King’s tent.
1 WATCHMAN. Come on, my masters, each man take his stand. The King by this is set him down to sleep.
2 WATCHMAN. What, will he not to bed?
1 WATCHMAN. Why, no; for he hath made a solemn vow Never to lie and take his natural rest Till Warwick or himself be quite suppressed.
2 WATCHMAN. Tomorrow, then, belike shall be the day, If Warwick be so near as men report.
3 WATCHMAN. But say, I pray, what nobleman is that That with the King here resteth in his tent?
1 WATCHMAN. ’Tis the Lord Hastings, the King’s chiefest friend.
3 WATCHMAN. O, is it so? But why commands the King That his chief followers lodge in towns about him, While he himself keeps in the cold field?
2 WATCHMAN. ’Tis the more honour, because more dangerous.
3 WATCHMAN. Ay, but give me worship and quietness; I like it better than dangerous honour. If Warwick knew in what estate he stands, ’Tis to be doubted he would waken him.
1 WATCHMAN. Unless our halberds did shut up his passage.
2 WATCHMAN. Ay, wherefore else guard we his royal tent But to defend his person from night-foes?
Enter Warwick, George (Duke of Clarence), Oxford, Somerset and French Soldiers, silent all.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: This is his tent; and see where stand his guard.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Courage, my masters! Honour now or never!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But follow me, and Edward shall be ours.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: 1 WATCHMAN.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Who goes there?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: 2 WATCHMAN.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Stay, or thou diest.
[_Warwick and the rest cry all, “Warwick! Warwick!” and set upon the guard, who fly, crying “Arm! Arm!” Warwick  and the rest following them._]

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: The drum playing and trumpet sounding, enter Warwick, Somerset, and the

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: rest, bringing the King out in his gown, sitting in a chair. Richard

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: (Duke of Gloucester) and Hastings fly over the stage.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: What are they that fly there?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Richard and Hastings.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Let them go. Here is the Duke.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: The Duke? Why, Warwick, when we parted,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Thou call’dst me king?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Ay, but the case is altered.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: When you disgraced me in my embassade,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Then I degraded you from being king,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And come now to create you Duke of York.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Alas, how should you govern any kingdom

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That know not how to use ambassadors,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Nor how to be contented with one wife,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Nor how to use your brothers brotherly,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Nor how to study for the people’s welfare,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Nor how to shroud yourself from enemies?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Yea, brother of Clarence, art thou here too?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Nay, then I see that Edward needs must down.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Yet, Warwick, in despite of all mischance

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Of thee thyself and all thy complices,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Edward will always bear himself as king.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Though Fortune’s malice overthrow my state,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: My mind exceeds the compass of her wheel.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Then for his mind be Edward England’s king;
[_Takes off his crown._]

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But Henry now shall wear the English crown

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And be true king indeed, thou but the shadow.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: My lord of Somerset, at my request,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: See that forthwith Duke Edward be conveyed

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Unto my brother, Archbishop of York.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: When I have fought with Pembroke and his fellows,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I’ll follow you and tell what answer

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Lewis and the Lady Bona send to him.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Now, for a while farewell, good Duke of York.
[_They begin to lead him out forcibly._]

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: What fates impose, that men must needs abide;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: It boots not to resist both wind and tide.
[_Exit King Edward, led out; Somerset with him._]

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: What now remains, my lords, for us to do,

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: But march to London with our soldiers?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Ay, that’s the first thing that we have to do,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: To free King Henry from imprisonment

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And see him seated in the regal throne.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Queen Elizabeth and Rivers.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Madam, what makes you in this sudden change?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Why, brother Rivers, are you yet to learn

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: What late misfortune is befall’n King Edward?

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: What, loss of some pitched battle against Warwick?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: No, but the loss of his own royal person.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Then is my sovereign slain?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Ay, almost slain, for he is taken prisoner,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Either betrayed by falsehood of his guard

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Or by his foe surprised at unawares;

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: And, as I further have to understand,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Is new committed to the Bishop of York,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Fell Warwick’s brother and by that our foe.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: These news, I must confess, are full of grief;

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Yet, gracious madam, bear it as you may.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Warwick may lose that now hath won the day.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Till then, fair hope must hinder life’s decay;

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: And I the rather wean me from despair

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: For love of Edward’s offspring in my womb.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: This is it that makes me bridle passion

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: And bear with mildness my misfortune’s cross,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Ay, ay, for this I draw in many a tear

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: And stop the rising of blood-sucking sighs,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Lest with my sighs or tears I blast or drown

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: King Edward’s fruit, true heir to th’ English crown.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: But, madam, where is Warwick then become?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: I am informed that he comes towards London

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: To set the crown once more on Henry’s head.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Guess thou the rest: King Edward’s friends must down.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: But to prevent the tyrant’s violence—

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: For trust not him that hath once broken faith—

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: I’ll hence forthwith unto the sanctuary

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: To save at least the heir of Edward’s right.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: There shall I rest secure from force and fraud.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Come, therefore, let us fly while we may fly.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: If Warwick take us, we are sure to die.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A park near Middleham Castle in Yorkshire

lines.text: Enter Richard (Duke of Gloucester), Lord Hastings, Sir William Stanley and others.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Now, my Lord Hastings and Sir William Stanley,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Leave off to wonder why I drew you hither

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Into this chiefest thicket of the park.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Thus stands the case: you know our King, my brother,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Is prisoner to the Bishop here, at whose hands

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: He hath good usage and great liberty,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And often but attended with weak guard,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Comes hunting this way to disport himself.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I have advertised him by secret means

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That if about this hour he make this way,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Under the colour of his usual game,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: He shall here find his friends with horse and men

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To set him free from his captivity.
Enter King Edward and a Huntsman with him.

lines.speaker: HUNTSMAN
lines.text: This way, my lord, for this way lies the game.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Nay, this way, man. See where the huntsmen stand.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Now, brother of Gloucester, Lord Hastings, and the rest,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Stand you thus close to steal the Bishop’s deer?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Brother, the time and case requireth haste;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Your horse stands ready at the park corner.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: But whither shall we then?

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: To Lynn, my lord, and shipped from thence to Flanders.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Well guessed, believe me, for that was my meaning.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Stanley, I will requite thy forwardness.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But wherefore stay we? ’Tis no time to talk.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Huntsman, what sayst thou? Wilt thou go along?

lines.speaker: HUNTSMAN
lines.text: Better do so than tarry and be hanged.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Come then, away! Let’s ha’ no more ado.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Bishop, farewell; shield thee from Warwick’s frown,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And pray that I may repossess the crown.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter King Henry, George (Duke of Clarence), Warwick, Somerset, young Richmond, Oxford, Montague, and Lieutenant of the Tower.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Master Lieutenant, now that God and friends

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Have shaken Edward from the regal seat

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And turned my captive state to liberty,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My fear to hope, my sorrows unto joys,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: At our enlargement what are thy due fees?

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: Subjects may challenge nothing of their sovereigns;

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: But if an humble prayer may prevail,

lines.speaker: LIEUTENANT
lines.text: I then crave pardon of your Majesty.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For what, lieutenant? For well using me?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Nay, be thou sure I’ll well requite thy kindness,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For that it made my imprisonment a pleasure;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ay, such a pleasure as incaged birds

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Conceive when, after many moody thoughts,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: At last by notes of household harmony

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: They quite forget their loss of liberty.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But, Warwick, after God thou sett’st me free,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And chiefly therefore I thank God and thee;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: He was the author, thou the instrument.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Therefore, that I may conquer Fortune’s spite,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: By living low where Fortune cannot hurt me,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And that the people of this blessed land

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: May not be punished with my thwarting stars,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Warwick, although my head still wear the crown,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I here resign my government to thee,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For thou art fortunate in all thy deeds.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Your Grace hath still been famed for virtuous,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And now may seem as wise as virtuous

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: By spying and avoiding Fortune’s malice,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For few men rightly temper with the stars;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Yet in this one thing let me blame your Grace,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For choosing me when Clarence is in place.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: No, Warwick, thou art worthy of the sway,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: To whom the heavens in thy nativity

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Adjudged an olive branch and laurel crown,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: As likely to be blest in peace and war;

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: And therefore I yield thee my free consent.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And I choose Clarence only for Protector.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Warwick and Clarence, give me both your hands.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Now join your hands, and with your hands your hearts,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That no dissension hinder government.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I make you both Protectors of this land,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: While I myself will lead a private life

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And in devotion spend my latter days,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To sin’s rebuke and my Creator’s praise.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: What answers Clarence to his sovereign’s will?

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: That he consents, if Warwick yield consent,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: For on thy fortune I repose myself.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Why, then, though loath, yet I must be content.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: We’ll yoke together, like a double shadow

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: To Henry’s body, and supply his place;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I mean, in bearing weight of government,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: While he enjoys the honour and his ease.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And, Clarence, now then it is more than needful

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Forthwith that Edward be pronounced a traitor

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And all his lands and goods be confiscate.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: What else? And that succession be determined.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Ay, therein Clarence shall not want his part.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But with the first of all your chief affairs

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Let me entreat—for I command no more—

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That Margaret your Queen and my son Edward

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Be sent for to return from France with speed;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For till I see them here, by doubtful fear

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My joy of liberty is half eclipsed.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: It shall be done, my sovereign, with all speed.
