lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My Lord of Somerset, what youth is that

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Of whom you seem to have so tender care?

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: My liege, it is young Henry, Earl of Richmond.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Come hither, England’s hope. If secret powers
[_Lays his hand on his head._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Suggest but truth to my divining thoughts,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: This pretty lad will prove our country’s bliss.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: His looks are full of peaceful majesty,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: His head by nature framed to wear a crown,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: His hand to wield a sceptre, and himself

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Likely in time to bless a regal throne.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Make much of him, my lords, for this is he

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Must help you more than you are hurt by me.
Enter a Post.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: What news, my friend?

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: That Edward is escaped from your brother

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: And fled, as he hears since, to Burgundy.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Unsavoury news! But how made he escape?

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: He was conveyed by Richard, Duke of Gloucester

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: And the Lord Hastings, who attended him

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: In secret ambush on the forest side

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: And from the Bishop’s huntsmen rescued him,

lines.speaker: POST
lines.text: For hunting was his daily exercise.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: My brother was too careless of his charge.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But let us hence, my sovereign, to provide

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: A salve for any sore that may betide.
[_Exeunt all but Somerset, Richmond and Oxford._]

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: My lord, I like not of this flight of Edward’s,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: For doubtless Burgundy will yield him help,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: And we shall have more wars before ’t be long.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: As Henry’s late presaging prophecy

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Did glad my heart with hope of this young Richmond,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: So doth my heart misgive me, in these conflicts

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: What may befall him, to his harm and ours.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Therefore, Lord Oxford, to prevent the worst,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Forthwith we’ll send him hence to Brittany

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Till storms be past of civil enmity.

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Ay, for if Edward repossess the crown,

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: ’Tis like that Richmond with the rest shall down.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: It shall be so. He shall to Brittany.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Come therefore, let’s about it speedily.
[_Exeunt._]
Flourish. Enter King Edward, Richard (Duke of Gloucester), Hastings and Soldiers.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Now, brother Richard, Lord Hastings, and the rest,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Yet thus far Fortune maketh us amends,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And says that once more I shall interchange

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: My waned state for Henry’s regal crown.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Well have we passed and now repassed the seas,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And brought desired help from Burgundy.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: What then remains, we being thus arrived

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: From Ravenspurgh haven before the gates of York,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: But that we enter as into our dukedom?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The gates made fast! Brother, I like not this;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For many men that stumble at the threshold

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Are well foretold that danger lurks within.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Tush, man, abodements must not now affright us.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: By fair or foul means we must enter in,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: For hither will our friends repair to us.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: My liege, I’ll knock once more to summon them.
Enter on the walls, the Mayor of York and his Brethren.

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: My lords, we were forewarned of your coming

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: And shut the gates for safety of ourselves,

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: For now we owe allegiance unto Henry.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: But, master Mayor, if Henry be your king,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Yet Edward, at the least, is Duke of York.

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: True, my good lord, I know you for no less.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Why, and I challenge nothing but my dukedom,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: As being well content with that alone.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But when the fox hath once got in his nose,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: He’ll soon find means to make the body follow.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Why, master Mayor, why stand you in a doubt?

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Open the gates; we are King Henry’s friends.

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Ay, say you so? The gates shall then be opened.
[_He descends._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: A wise, stout captain, and soon persuaded.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: The good old man would fain that all were well,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: So ’twere not long of him; but, being entered,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I doubt not, I, but we shall soon persuade

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Both him and all his brothers unto reason.
Enter the Mayor and two Aldermen below.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: So, master Mayor, these gates must not be shut

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: But in the night or in the time of war.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: What, fear not, man, but yield me up the keys;
[_Takes his keys._]

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: For Edward will defend the town and thee

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And all those friends that deign to follow me.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: March. Enter Montgomery with drum and Soldiers.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Brother, this is Sir John Montgomery,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Our trusty friend unless I be deceived.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Welcome, Sir John! But why come you in arms?

lines.speaker: MONTGOMERY
lines.text: To help King Edward in his time of storm,

lines.speaker: MONTGOMERY
lines.text: As every loyal subject ought to do.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Thanks, good Montgomery; but we now forget

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Our title to the crown, and only claim

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Our dukedom till God please to send the rest.

lines.speaker: MONTGOMERY
lines.text: Then fare you well, for I will hence again.

lines.speaker: MONTGOMERY
lines.text: I came to serve a king, and not a duke.

lines.speaker: MONTGOMERY
lines.text: Drummer, strike up, and let us march away.
[_The drum begins to march._]

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Nay, stay, Sir John, a while, and we’ll debate

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: By what safe means the crown may be recovered.

lines.speaker: MONTGOMERY
lines.text: What talk you of debating? In few words,

lines.speaker: MONTGOMERY
lines.text: If you’ll not here proclaim yourself our king,

lines.speaker: MONTGOMERY
lines.text: I’ll leave you to your fortune and be gone

lines.speaker: MONTGOMERY
lines.text: To keep them back that come to succour you.

lines.speaker: MONTGOMERY
lines.text: Why shall we fight if you pretend no title?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Why, brother, wherefore stand you on nice points?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: When we grow stronger, then we’ll make our claim.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Till then ’tis wisdom to conceal our meaning.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Away with scrupulous wit! Now arms must rule.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And fearless minds climb soonest unto crowns.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Brother, we will proclaim you out of hand;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The bruit thereof will bring you many friends.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Then be it as you will; for ’tis my right,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And Henry but usurps the diadem.

lines.speaker: MONTGOMERY
lines.text: Ay, now my sovereign speaketh like himself,

lines.speaker: MONTGOMERY
lines.text: And now will I be Edward’s champion.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Sound, trumpet; Edward shall be here proclaimed.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Come, fellow soldier, make thou proclamation.
[_Gives him a paper. Flourish._]
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: SOLDIER
lines.text: _Edward the Fourth, by the Grace of God, King of England and

lines.speaker: SOLDIER
lines.text: France, and Lord of Ireland, etc._

lines.speaker: MONTGOMERY
lines.text: And whoso’er gainsays King Edward’s right,

lines.speaker: MONTGOMERY
lines.text: By this I challenge him to single fight.
[_Throws down his gauntlet._]

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Long live Edward the Fourth!

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Thanks, brave Montgomery, and thanks unto you all.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: If Fortune serve me, I’ll requite this kindness.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Now for this night let’s harbour here in York,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And when the morning sun shall raise his car

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Above the border of this horizon

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: We’ll forward towards Warwick and his mates;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: For well I wot that Henry is no soldier.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Ah, froward Clarence, how evil it beseems thee

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: To flatter Henry and forsake thy brother!

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Yet, as we may, we’ll meet both thee and Warwick.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Come on, brave soldiers; doubt not of the day,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And, that once gotten, doubt not of large pay.
[_Exeunt._]
Flourish. Enter King Henry, Warwick, Montague, George (Duke of Clarence), Oxford and Exeter.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: What counsel, lords? Edward from Belgia,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: With hasty Germans and blunt Hollanders,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Hath passed in safety through the Narrow Seas,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And with his troops doth march amain to London;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And many giddy people flock to him.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Let’s levy men and beat him back again.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: A little fire is quickly trodden out,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Which, being suffered, rivers cannot quench.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: In Warwickshire I have true-hearted friends,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Not mutinous in peace, yet bold in war.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Those will I muster up; and thou, son Clarence,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Shalt stir up in Suffolk, Norfolk, and in Kent

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: The knights and gentlemen to come with thee.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Thou, brother Montague, in Buckingham,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Northampton, and in Leicestershire shalt find

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Men well inclined to hear what thou command’st.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And thou, brave Oxford, wondrous well beloved,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: In Oxfordshire shalt muster up thy friends.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: My sovereign, with the loving citizens,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Like to his island girt in with the ocean,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Or modest Dian circled with her nymphs,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Shall rest in London till we come to him.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Fair lords, take leave and stand not to reply.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Farewell, my sovereign.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Farewell, my Hector, and my Troy’s true hope.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: In sign of truth, I kiss your Highness’ hand.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Well-minded Clarence, be thou fortunate.

lines.speaker: MONTAGUE
lines.text: Comfort, my lord; and so I take my leave.

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: And thus [_kissing Henry’s hand_] I seal my truth, and bid adieu.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Sweet Oxford, and my loving Montague,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And all at once, once more a happy farewell.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Farewell, sweet lords; let’s meet at Coventry.
[_Exeunt all but King Henry and Exeter._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Here at the palace will I rest a while.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Cousin of Exeter, what thinks your lordship?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Methinks the power that Edward hath in field

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Should not be able to encounter mine.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: The doubt is that he will seduce the rest.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That’s not my fear; my meed hath got me fame.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I have not stopped mine ears to their demands,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Nor posted off their suits with slow delays;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My pity hath been balm to heal their wounds,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My mildness hath allayed their swelling griefs,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My mercy dried their water-flowing tears.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I have not been desirous of their wealth

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Nor much oppressed them with great subsidies,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Nor forward of revenge, though they much erred.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Then why should they love Edward more than me?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No, Exeter, these graces challenge grace;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And when the lion fawns upon the lamb,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The lamb will never cease to follow him.
[_Shout within “A York! A York!”_]

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Hark, hark, my lord, what shouts are these?
Enter King Edward, Richard (Duke of Gloucester) and Soldiers.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Seize on the shame-faced Henry, bear him hence,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And once again proclaim us King of England.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: You are the fount that makes small brooks to flow.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Now stops thy spring; my sea shall suck them dry

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And swell so much the higher by their ebb.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Hence with him to the Tower. Let him not speak.
[_Exeunt some with King Henry._]

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And, lords, towards Coventry bend we our course,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Where peremptory Warwick now remains.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: The sun shines hot, and, if we use delay,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Cold biting winter mars our hoped-for hay.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Away betimes, before his forces join,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And take the great-grown traitor unawares.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Brave warriors, march amain towards Coventry.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter, Warwick, the Mayor of Coventry, two Messengers and others, upon the walls.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Where is the post that came from valiant Oxford?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: How far hence is thy lord, mine honest fellow?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: 1 MESSENGER.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: By this at Dunsmore, marching hitherward.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: How far off is our brother Montague?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Where is the post that came from Montague?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: 2 MESSENGER.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: By this at Daintry, with a puissant troop.
Enter Sir John Somerville.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Say, Somerville, what says my loving son?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And, by thy guess, how nigh is Clarence now?

lines.speaker: SOMERVILLE
lines.text: At Southam I did leave him with his forces

lines.speaker: SOMERVILLE
lines.text: And do expect him here some two hours hence.
[_Drum heard._]

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Then Clarence is at hand; I hear his drum.

lines.speaker: SOMERVILLE
lines.text: It is not his, my lord; here Southam lies.

lines.speaker: SOMERVILLE
lines.text: The drum your honour hears marcheth from Warwick.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Who should that be? Belike, unlooked-for friends.

lines.speaker: SOMERVILLE
lines.text: They are at hand, and you shall quickly know.

lines.speaker: SOMERVILLE
lines.text: March. Flourish. Enter King Edward, Richard (Duke of Gloucester) and

lines.speaker: SOMERVILLE
lines.text: Soldiers.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Go, trumpet, to the walls and sound a parle.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: See how the surly Warwick mans the wall.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: O, unbid spite! Is sportful Edward come?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Where slept our scouts, or how are they seduced,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That we could hear no news of his repair?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Now, Warwick, wilt thou ope the city gates,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Speak gentle words and humbly bend thy knee?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Call Edward King and at his hands beg mercy,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And he shall pardon thee these outrages.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Nay, rather, wilt thou draw thy forces hence,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Confess who set thee up and plucked thee down,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Call Warwick patron and be penitent,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And thou shalt still remain the Duke of York.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I thought, at least, he would have said the King;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Or did he make the jest against his will?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Is not a dukedom, sir, a goodly gift?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Ay, by my faith, for a poor earl to give;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I’ll do thee service for so good a gift.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: ’Twas I that gave the kingdom to thy brother.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Why, then, ’tis mine, if but by Warwick’s gift.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Thou art no Atlas for so great a weight;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And, weakling, Warwick takes his gift again;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And Henry is my King, Warwick his subject.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: But Warwick’s king is Edward’s prisoner;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And, gallant Warwick, do but answer this:

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: What is the body when the head is off?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Alas, that Warwick had no more forecast,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But, whiles he thought to steal the single ten,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The king was slily fingered from the deck!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: You left poor Henry at the Bishop’s palace,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And ten to one you’ll meet him in the Tower.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: ’Tis even so; yet you are Warwick still.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Come, Warwick, take the time; kneel down, kneel down.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Nay, when? Strike now, or else the iron cools.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I had rather chop this hand off at a blow

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And with the other fling it at thy face,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Than bear so low a sail to strike to thee.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Sail how thou canst, have wind and tide thy friend,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: This hand, fast wound about thy coal-black hair,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Shall, whiles thy head is warm and new cut off,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Write in the dust this sentence with thy blood:

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: “Wind-changing Warwick now can change no more.”
Enter Oxford with drum and colours.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: O cheerful colours! See where Oxford comes!

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Oxford, Oxford, for Lancaster!
[_He and his forces enter the city._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The gates are open; let us enter too.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: So other foes may set upon our backs.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Stand we in good array, for they no doubt

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Will issue out again and bid us battle;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: If not, the city being but of small defence,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: We’ll quietly rouse the traitors in the same.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: O, welcome, Oxford, for we want thy help.
Enter Montague with drum and colours.

lines.speaker: MONTAGUE
lines.text: Montague, Montague, for Lancaster!
[_He and his forces enter the city._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Thou and thy brother both shall buy this treason

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Even with the dearest blood your bodies bear.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: The harder matched, the greater victory.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: My mind presageth happy gain and conquest.
Enter Somerset with drum and colours.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Somerset, Somerset, for Lancaster!
[_He and his forces enter the city._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Two of thy name, both Dukes of Somerset,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Have sold their lives unto the House of York;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And thou shalt be the third if this sword hold.
Enter George (Duke of Clarence) with drum and colours.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And lo, where George of Clarence sweeps along,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Of force enough to bid his brother battle;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: With whom an upright zeal to right prevails

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: More than the nature of a brother’s love.
[_Richard and George whisper._]

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Come, Clarence, come; thou wilt if Warwick call.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Father of Warwick, know you what this means?
[_Taking the red rose from his hat and throws the rose at Warwick._]

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Look here, I throw my infamy at thee.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: I will not ruinate my father’s house,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Who gave his blood to lime the stones together,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: And set up Lancaster. Why, trowest thou, Warwick,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: That Clarence is so harsh, so blunt, unnatural,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: To bend the fatal instruments of war

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Against his brother and his lawful King?

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Perhaps thou wilt object my holy oath.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: To keep that oath were more impiety

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Than Jephthah’s when he sacrificed his daughter.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: I am so sorry for my trespass made

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: That, to deserve well at my brother’s hands,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: I here proclaim myself thy mortal foe,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: With resolution, whereso’er I meet thee—

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: As I will meet thee if thou stir abroad—

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: To plague thee for thy foul misleading me.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: And so, proud-hearted Warwick, I defy thee,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: And to my brother turn my blushing cheeks.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Pardon me, Edward, I will make amends.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: And, Richard, do not frown upon my faults,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: For I will henceforth be no more unconstant.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Now, welcome more, and ten times more beloved,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Than if thou never hadst deserved our hate.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Welcome, good Clarence; this is brother-like.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: O passing traitor, perjured and unjust!

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: What, Warwick, wilt thou leave the town and fight?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Or shall we beat the stones about thine ears?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Alas! I am not cooped here for defence!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I will away towards Barnet presently

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And bid thee battle, Edward, if thou dar’st.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Yes, Warwick, Edward dares, and leads the way.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Lords, to the field! Saint George and victory!
[_Exeunt. March. Warwick and his company follows._]

scenes.setting: A Field of Battle near Barnet

lines.text: Alarum and excursions. Enter King Edward bringing forth Warwick wounded.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: So, lie thou there. Die thou, and die our fear,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: For Warwick was a bug that feared us all.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Now, Montague, sit fast; I seek for thee,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: That Warwick’s bones may keep thine company.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Ah, who is nigh? Come to me, friend or foe,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And tell me who is victor, York or Warwick?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Why ask I that? My mangled body shows,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: My blood, my want of strength, my sick heart shows

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That I must yield my body to the earth

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And, by my fall, the conquest to my foe.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Thus yields the cedar to the axe’s edge,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Whose arms gave shelter to the princely eagle,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Under whose shade the ramping lion slept,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Whose top branch overpeered Jove’s spreading tree,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And kept low shrubs from winter’s pow’rful wind.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: These eyes, that now are dimmed with death’s black veil,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Have been as piercing as the midday sun,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: To search the secret treasons of the world;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: The wrinkles in my brows, now filled with blood,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Were likened oft to kingly sepulchres,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For who lived King but I could dig his grave?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And who durst smile when Warwick bent his brow?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Lo, now my glory smeared in dust and blood!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: My parks, my walks, my manors that I had,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Even now forsake me; and of all my lands

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Is nothing left me but my body’s length.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Why, what is pomp, rule, reign, but earth and dust?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And live we how we can, yet die we must.
Enter Oxford and Somerset.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Ah, Warwick, Warwick, wert thou as we are,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: We might recover all our loss again.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: The Queen from France hath brought a puissant power;

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Even now we heard the news. Ah, couldst thou fly!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Why, then I would not fly. Ah, Montague!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: If thou be there, sweet brother, take my hand

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And with thy lips keep in my soul awhile.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Thou lov’st me not; for, brother, if thou didst,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Thy tears would wash this cold congealed blood

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That glues my lips and will not let me speak.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Come quickly, Montague, or I am dead.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Ah, Warwick, Montague hath breathed his last,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: And to the latest gasp cried out for Warwick,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: And said “Commend me to my valiant brother.”

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: And more he would have said, and more he spoke,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Which sounded like a cannon in a vault,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: That mought not be distinguished; but at last

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: I well might hear, delivered with a groan,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: “O farewell, Warwick!”

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Sweet rest his soul! Fly, lords, and save yourselves,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For Warwick bids you all farewell, to meet in heaven.
[_He dies._]

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Away, away, to meet the Queen’s great power!
[_Here they bear away his body. Exeunt._]
Flourish. Enter King Edward in triumph, with Richard, George and the rest.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Thus far our fortune keeps an upward course,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And we are graced with wreaths of victory.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: But in the midst of this bright-shining day,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: I spy a black, suspicious, threat’ning cloud

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: That will encounter with our glorious sun

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Ere he attain his easeful western bed.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: I mean, my lords, those powers that the Queen

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Hath raised in Gallia have arrived our coast

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And, as we hear, march on to fight with us.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: A little gale will soon disperse that cloud

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: And blow it to the source from whence it came;

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Thy very beams will dry those vapours up,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: For every cloud engenders not a storm.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The Queen is valued thirty thousand strong,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And Somerset, with Oxford, fled to her.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: If she have time to breathe, be well assured

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Her faction will be full as strong as ours.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: We are advertised by our loving friends

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: That they do hold their course toward Tewkesbury.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: We, having now the best at Barnet field,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Will thither straight, for willingness rids way;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And, as we march, our strength will be augmented

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: In every county as we go along.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Strike up the drum! cry “Courage!” and away.
[_Exeunt._]
Flourish. March. Enter Queen Margaret, Prince Edward, Somerset, Oxford and Soldiers.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Great lords, wise men ne’er sit and wail their loss,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But cheerly seek how to redress their harms.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What though the mast be now blown overboard,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The cable broke, the holding-anchor lost,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And half our sailors swallowed in the flood?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Yet lives our pilot still. Is ’t meet that he

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Should leave the helm and, like a fearful lad,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: With tearful eyes add water to the sea

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And give more strength to that which hath too much,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Whiles in his moan the ship splits on the rock,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Which industry and courage might have saved?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ah, what a shame, ah, what a fault were this!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Say Warwick was our anchor; what of that?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And Montague our topmast; what of him?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Our slaughtered friends the tackles; what of these?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Why, is not Oxford here another anchor?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And Somerset another goodly mast?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The friends of France our shrouds and tacklings?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And, though unskilful, why not Ned and I

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: For once allowed the skilful pilot’s charge?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: We will not from the helm to sit and weep,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But keep our course, though the rough wind say no,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: From shelves and rocks that threaten us with wrack.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: As good to chide the waves as speak them fair.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And what is Edward but a ruthless sea?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What Clarence but a quicksand of deceit?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And Richard but a ragged fatal rock?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: All these the enemies to our poor bark?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Say you can swim: alas, ’tis but a while!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Tread on the sand: why, there you quickly sink;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Bestride the rock: the tide will wash you off,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Or else you famish; that’s a threefold death.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: This speak I, lords, to let you understand,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: If case some one of you would fly from us,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: That there’s no hoped-for mercy with the brothers

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: More than with ruthless waves, with sands, and rocks.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Why, courage then! What cannot be avoided

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: ’Twere childish weakness to lament or fear.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Methinks a woman of this valiant spirit

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Should, if a coward heard her speak these words,

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Infuse his breast with magnanimity

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: And make him, naked, foil a man at arms.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: I speak not this as doubting any here;

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: For did I but suspect a fearful man,

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: He should have leave to go away betimes,

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Lest in our need he might infect another

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: And make him of the like spirit to himself.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: If any such be here, as God forbid!

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Let him depart before we need his help.

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Women and children of so high a courage,

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: And warriors faint! Why, ’twere perpetual shame.

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: O, brave young Prince, thy famous grandfather

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Doth live again in thee. Long mayst thou live

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: To bear his image and renew his glories!

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: And he that will not fight for such a hope,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Go home to bed and, like the owl by day,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: If he arise, be mocked and wondered at.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thanks, gentle Somerset. Sweet Oxford, thanks.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: And take his thanks that yet hath nothing else.
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Prepare you, lords, for Edward is at hand

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Ready to fight; therefore be resolute.

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: I thought no less. It is his policy

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: To haste thus fast, to find us unprovided.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: But he’s deceived; we are in readiness.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: This cheers my heart, to see your forwardness.

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Here pitch our battle; hence we will not budge.
Flourish and march. Enter King Edward, Richard, George and Soldiers.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Brave followers, yonder stands the thorny wood

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Which by the heaven’s assistance and your strength

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Must by the roots be hewn up yet ere night.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: I need not add more fuel to your fire,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: For, well I wot, ye blaze to burn them out.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Give signal to the fight, and to it, lords!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Lords, knights, and gentlemen, what I should say

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: My tears gainsay; for every word I speak

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ye see I drink the water of my eye.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Therefore, no more but this: Henry, your sovereign,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Is prisoner to the foe, his state usurped,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: His realm a slaughter-house, his subjects slain,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: His statutes cancelled, and his treasure spent;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And yonder is the wolf that makes this spoil.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: You fight in justice. Then, in God’s name, lords,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Be valiant and give signal to the fight.
[_Alarum, retreat, excursions. Exeunt both armies_]
Flourish. Enter King Edward, Richard, George and Soldiers; with Queen Margaret, Oxford and Somerset as prisoners.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Now here a period of tumultuous broils.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Away with Oxford to Hames Castle straight.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: For Somerset, off with his guilty head.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Go, bear them hence; I will not hear them speak.

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: For my part, I’ll not trouble thee with words.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Nor I, but stoop with patience to my fortune.
[_Exeunt Oxford and Somerset, guarded._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: So part we sadly in this troublous world,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: To meet with joy in sweet Jerusalem.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Is proclamation made that who finds Edward

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Shall have a high reward, and he his life?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: It is, and lo where youthful Edward comes.
Enter soldiers with Prince Edward.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Bring forth the gallant; let us hear him speak.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: What, can so young a man begin to prick?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Edward, what satisfaction canst thou make

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: For bearing arms, for stirring up my subjects,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And all the trouble thou hast turned me to?

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Speak like a subject, proud, ambitious York.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Suppose that I am now my father’s mouth;

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Resign thy chair, and where I stand kneel thou,

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Whilst I propose the selfsame words to thee

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Which, traitor, thou wouldst have me answer to.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ah, thy father had been so resolved!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That you might still have worn the petticoat

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And ne’er have stol’n the breech from Lancaster.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Let Aesop fable in a winter’s night;

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: His currish riddle sorts not with this place.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: By heaven, brat, I’ll plague you for that word.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ay, thou wast born to be a plague to men.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For God’s sake, take away this captive scold.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Nay, take away this scolding crookback rather.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Peace, wilful boy, or I will charm your tongue.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Untutored lad, thou art too malapert.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: I know my duty; you are all undutiful.

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: Lascivious Edward, and thou perjured George,

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: And thou misshapen Dick, I tell ye all

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: I am your better, traitors as ye are,

lines.speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
lines.text: And thou usurp’st my father’s right and mine.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Take that, the likeness of this railer here.
[_Stabs him._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Sprawl’st thou? Take that to end thy agony.
[_Stabs him._]

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: And there’s for twitting me with perjury.
[_Stabs him._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: O, kill me too!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Marry, and shall.
[_Offers to kill her._]

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Hold, Richard, hold; for we have done too much.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Why should she live to fill the world with words?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: What, doth she swoon? Use means for her recovery.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Clarence, excuse me to the King my brother.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I’ll hence to London on a serious matter.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Ere ye come there, be sure to hear some news.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: What? What?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The Tower, the Tower!
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: O Ned, sweet Ned, speak to thy mother, boy.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Canst thou not speak? O traitors, murderers!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: They that stabbed Caesar shed no blood at all,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Did not offend, nor were not worthy blame,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: If this foul deed were by to equal it.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: He was a man; this, in respect, a child,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And men ne’er spend their fury on a child.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What’s worse than murderer, that I may name it?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: No, no, my heart will burst an if I speak;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And I will speak, that so my heart may burst.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Butchers and villains, bloody cannibals!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: How sweet a plant have you untimely cropped!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: You have no children, butchers; if you had,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The thought of them would have stirred up remorse.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But if you ever chance to have a child,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Look in his youth to have him so cut off

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: As, deathsmen, you have rid this sweet young prince!

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Away with her; go bear her hence perforce.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Nay, never bear me hence, dispatch me here.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Here sheathe thy sword; I’ll pardon thee my death.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What, wilt thou not? Then, Clarence, do it thou.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: By heaven, I will not do thee so much ease.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Good Clarence, do; sweet Clarence, do thou do it.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Didst thou not hear me swear I would not do it?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ay, but thou usest to forswear thyself.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: ’Twas sin before, but now ’tis charity.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What, wilt thou not? Where is that devil’s butcher, Richard,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Hard-favoured Richard? Richard, where art thou?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thou art not here. Murder is thy alms-deed;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Petitioners for blood thou ne’er putt’st back.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Away, I say! I charge ye, bear her hence.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: So come to you and yours as to this prince!
[_She is taken out._]

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Where’s Richard gone?

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: To London all in post, and, as I guess,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: To make a bloody supper in the Tower.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: He’s sudden if a thing comes in his head.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Now march we hence. Discharge the common sort

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: With pay and thanks, and let’s away to London

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And see our gentle Queen how well she fares.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: By this, I hope, she hath a son for me.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter King Henry and Richard, with the Lieutenant on the walls.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Good day, my lord. What, at your book so hard?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ay, my good lord—my lord, I should say rather.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: ’Tis sin to flatter; “good” was little better:

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: “Good Gloucester” and “good devil” were alike,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And both preposterous; therefore, not “good lord”.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Sirrah, leave us to ourselves; we must confer.
[_Exit Lieutenant._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So flies the reckless shepherd from the wolf;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So first the harmless sheep doth yield his fleece,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And next his throat unto the butcher’s knife.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What scene of death hath Roscius now to act?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Suspicion always haunts the guilty mind;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The thief doth fear each bush an officer.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The bird that hath been limed in a bush

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: With trembling wings misdoubteth every bush;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And I, the hapless male to one sweet bird,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Have now the fatal object in my eye

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Where my poor young was limed, was caught, and killed.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Why, what a peevish fool was that of Crete

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That taught his son the office of a fowl!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And yet, for all his wings, the fool was drowned.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I, Daedalus; my poor boy, Icarus;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thy father, Minos, that denied our course;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The sun that seared the wings of my sweet boy,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thy brother Edward; and thyself, the sea

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whose envious gulf did swallow up his life.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ah, kill me with thy weapon, not with words!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My breast can better brook thy dagger’s point

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Than can my ears that tragic history.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But wherefore dost thou come? Is ’t for my life?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Think’st thou I am an executioner?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: A persecutor I am sure thou art.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If murdering innocents be executing,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Why, then thou art an executioner.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Thy son I killed for his presumption.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Hadst thou been killed when first thou didst presume,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thou hadst not lived to kill a son of mine.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And thus I prophesy: that many a thousand

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Which now mistrust no parcel of my fear,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And many an old man’s sigh, and many a widow’s,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And many an orphan’s water-standing eye,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Men for their sons’, wives for their husbands’,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Orphans for their parents’ timeless death,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Shall rue the hour that ever thou wast born.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The owl shrieked at thy birth, an evil sign;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The night-crow cried, aboding luckless time;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Dogs howled, and hideous tempest shook down trees;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The raven rooked her on the chimney’s top,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And chatt’ring pies in dismal discord sung;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thy mother felt more than a mother’s pain,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And yet brought forth less than a mother’s hope,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To wit, an indigested and deformed lump,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Not like the fruit of such a goodly tree.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Teeth hadst thou in thy head when thou wast born,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To signify thou cam’st to bite the world;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And, if the rest be true which I have heard,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thou cam’st—

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I’ll hear no more. Die, prophet, in thy speech.
[_Stabs him._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For this, amongst the rest, was I ordained.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ay, and for much more slaughter after this.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O God, forgive my sins, and pardon thee!
[_Dies._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: What, will the aspiring blood of Lancaster

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Sink in the ground? I thought it would have mounted.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: See how my sword weeps for the poor King’s death.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: O, may such purple tears be always shed

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: From those that wish the downfall of our house!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: If any spark of life be yet remaining,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Down, down to hell; and say I sent thee thither—
[_Stabs him again._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I that have neither pity, love, nor fear.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Indeed, ’tis true that Henry told me of,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For I have often heard my mother say

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I came into the world with my legs forward.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Had I not reason, think ye, to make haste

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And seek their ruin that usurped our right?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The midwife wondered, and the women cried

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: “O, Jesus bless us, he is born with teeth!”

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And so I was, which plainly signified

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That I should snarl, and bite, and play the dog.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Then, since the heavens have shaped my body so,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Let hell make crooked my mind to answer it.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I have no brother, I am like no brother;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And this word “love,” which greybeards call divine,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Be resident in men like one another,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And not in me. I am myself alone.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Clarence, beware; thou keep’st me from the light,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But I will sort a pitchy day for thee;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For I will buzz abroad such prophecies

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That Edward shall be fearful of his life;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And then, to purge his fear, I’ll be thy death.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: King Henry and the Prince his son are gone;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Clarence, thy turn is next, and then the rest,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Counting myself but bad till I be best.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I’ll throw thy body in another room,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And triumph, Henry, in thy day of doom.
[_Exit with the body._]
Flourish. Enter King Edward, Queen Elizabeth, George, Richard, Hastings, Nurse, carrying infant Prince Edward, and Attendants.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Once more we sit in England’s royal throne,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Repurchased with the blood of enemies.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: What valiant foemen, like to autumn’s corn,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Have we mowed down in tops of all their pride!

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Three Dukes of Somerset, threefold renowned

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: For hardy and undoubted champions;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Two Cliffords, as the father and the son;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And two Northumberlands; two braver men

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Ne’er spurred their coursers at the trumpet’s sound;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: With them the two brave bears, Warwick and Montague,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: That in their chains fettered the kingly lion

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And made the forest tremble when they roared.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Thus have we swept suspicion from our seat

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And made our footstool of security.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Come hither, Bess, and let me kiss my boy.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Young Ned, for thee thine uncles and myself

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Have in our armours watched the winter’s night,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Went all afoot in summer’s scalding heat,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: That thou mightst repossess the crown in peace;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And of our labours thou shalt reap the gain.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I’ll blast his harvest, if your head were laid;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For yet I am not looked on in the world.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: This shoulder was ordained so thick to heave,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And heave it shall some weight or break my back.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Work thou the way, and that shall execute.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Clarence and Gloucester, love my lovely Queen;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And kiss your princely nephew, brothers both.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: The duty that I owe unto your Majesty

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: I seal upon the lips of this sweet babe.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Thanks, noble Clarence; worthy brother, thanks.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And, that I love the tree from whence thou sprang’st,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Witness the loving kiss I give the fruit.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To say the truth, so Judas kissed his master

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And cried “All hail!” when as he meant all harm.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Now am I seated as my soul delights,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Having my country’s peace and brothers’ loves.

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: What will your Grace have done with Margaret?

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Reignier, her father, to the King of France

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: Hath pawned the Sicils and Jerusalem,

lines.speaker: GEORGE
lines.text: And hither have they sent it for her ransom.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Away with her and waft her hence to France.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And now what rests but that we spend the time

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: With stately triumphs, mirthful comic shows,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Such as befits the pleasure of the court?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Sound drums and trumpets! Farewell, sour annoy!

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: For here, I hope, begins our lasting joy.
[_Exeunt._]
